title: Comparison of the efficacy of three-dimensional printing-assisted strategy and traditional total ankle arthroplasty in the treatment of end-stage ankle arthritis.
abstract: Objective To compare perioperative parameters, early functional outcomes, and complication profiles between 3D printing-assisted total ankle arthroplasty strategy incorporating preoperative virtual planning, patient-specific osteotomy guides, and a customized talar component and conventional total ankle arthroplasty (TAA) in the treatment of end-stage ankle arthritis. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on data from 44 patients diagnosed with end-stage ankle arthritis who were admitted to our hospital between January 2021 and December 2023. Among them, 20 patients (observation group) underwent total ankle arthroplasty (TAA) using a 3D-printed patient-specific TAA strategy, while 24 patients (control group) received conventional TAA using the same tibial component and polyethylene liner but a standard off-the-shelf talar component, together with standard instrumentation. The following parameters were recorded and evaluated: operative duration, intraoperative blood loss, length of postoperative hospital stay, intraoperative fluoroscopy time, preoperative and postoperative American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) scores, visual analogue scale (VAS) scores, and ankle range of motion (ROM). Additionally, the occurrence of soft tissue-related complications was monitored. Results The AOFAS score, VAS score, and ankle range of motion (ROM) in both groups showed significant improvement postoperatively compared to preoperative values (P < 0.05). However, no statistically significant differences were observed between the two groups (P > 0.05). With regard to surgical outcomes, including operative time, intraoperative blood loss, postoperative hospitalization duration, and the intraoperative fluoroscopy time, the observation group demonstrated significantly better results than the control group (P < 0.001). Concerning postoperative complications, the observation group experienced only one case of superficial infection, whereas the control group had two cases of superficial infection and one case of wound edge necrosis. Although the total complication rate was slightly lower in the observation group, the difference between the two groups was not statistically significant (P = 0.389). Postoperative radiographic analysis confirmed significantly improved alignment accuracy of the tibial component in the observation group compared to the control group (P < 0.05). Conclusion The 3D printing-assisted TAA strategy appears to improve perioperative efficiency and short-term radiographic alignment accuracy compared with conventional TAA, whereas short-term functional outcomes and wound-related complication rates remain comparable between groups. Given the additional preoperative preparation time and cost, its theoretical promise for patients with complex deformities and its potential effect on long-term implant survival require further confirmation through prospective, randomized studies with long-term follow-up.

title: The 'Upstairs-Downstairs' heart with complete main pulmonary artery agenesis and PDA-dependent pulmonary circulation: A rare structural intersection characterized by multi detector computed tomography.
abstract: Superior-inferior ventricular arrangement is an exceedingly rare form of congenital cardiac malposition, representing fewer than 0.1% of all congenital heart diseases, and is almost invariably associated with complex intracardiac anomalies. We report a 3-year-old male who presented with persistent cyanosis, exertional dyspnea, and failure to thrive. Prospective ECG-gated CT angiography demonstrated situs solitus with levocardia. A superior-inferior ventricular arrangement was present, with the morphologic left ventricle positioned superior to the morphologic right ventricle. The great arteries were normally related, with a left-sided aortic arch. A large ventricular septal defect was identified. Pulmonary atresia was present, characterized by the absence of the right ventricular outflow tract, pulmonary valve, and main pulmonary artery. Native confluent branch pulmonary arteries were present and received pulmonary blood flow through a large patent ductus arteriosus supplying the left pulmonary artery, with additional small systemic-to-pulmonary collateral vessels. The morphologic right ventricle was dilated and hypertrophied, with associated enlargement of the right atrium. Pulmonary venous drainage was normal, and no abnormalities of the systemic venous drainage were identified. This case underscores the critical role of cardiac CT angiography in comprehensive anatomical delineation of rare and complex congenital cardiac malformations, with direct implications for surgical planning and prognostication.

title: Isolated cerebellopontine angle metastasis from breast cancer: The added value of MR spectroscopy.
abstract: Cerebellopontine angle (CPA) tumors are predominantly vestibular schwannomas and meningiomas; metastatic lesions in this location are rare, particularly in the absence of multiple brain metastases. We report the case of a 53-year-old woman with a history of invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast in HER2-positive metastatic relapse, in whom brain MRI revealed a single 28 × 24 mm mass in the right cerebellopontine angle. The lesion was isointense on T1- and T2-weighted images, contained fluid components, and showed restricted diffusion (ADC 0.64 × 10⁻³ mm²/s) with intense peripheral enhancement after gadolinium administration. MR spectroscopy demonstrated markedly elevated Cho/NAA (6.73) and Cho/Cr (5.72) ratios within the lesion, with a normal perilesional spectroscopic profile, favoring a secondary lesion and allowing the main differential diagnoses to be excluded without biopsy. The patient underwent stereotactic radiotherapy (30 Gy in 5 fractions), with significant regression of the lesion on follow-up MRI at five months. This case illustrates the role of MR spectroscopy in the non-invasive characterization of atypical cerebellopontine angle lesions.

title: Deep learning-based spot weight generation for online adaptive IMPT: implementation and technical feasibility on a clinical delivery system.
abstract: Purpose To investigate the feasibility of a deep learning-based method for generating intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) spot weights to enable a faster, more automated workflow. Methods A 3D Attention U-Net with a masked mean absolute error loss generated spot weights from four input channels (optimized plan dose, reference dose, CT image, spot mask), using planned spot weights as labels, and trained and tested on prostate, brain, and lung cases. Robustness was evaluated on target dose metrics only. The workflow was validated in the Eclipse® treatment planning system and delivered on a ProBeam 360° system. Results For weights in the range 0-5, mean absolute errors were below 0.8 for the prostate and brain models (15.9% and 48.1% of all weights, respectively) and below 1.7 for the lung model (31.2%). Mean relative errors were below 10% for the prostate model (5-65, 83.7%), 20% for the brain model (5-65, 51.7%), and 40% for the lung model (5-110, 68.6%); the remaining weights lay above these ranges and accounted for <0.5% of all weights. Gamma passing rates within the body contours (2%, 2 mm, 10% dose threshold) were 99.73 ± 0.32%, 98.95 ± 0.86%, and 92.75 ± 3.52% for the prostate, brain, and lung models, respectively. All delivered plans met the clinical QA acceptance criteria. Conclusion The proposed framework demonstrates the technical feasibility of generating IMPT spot weights with deep learning and implementing them on a clinical delivery system. Further improvement is needed for heterogeneous sites such as the lung.

Purpose

To investigate the feasibility of a deep learning-based method for generating intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) spot weights to enable a faster, more automated workflow.

Methods

A 3D Attention U-Net with a masked mean absolute error loss generated spot weights from four input channels (optimized plan dose, reference dose, CT image, spot mask), using planned spot weights as labels, and trained and tested on prostate, brain, and lung cases. Robustness was evaluated on target dose metrics only. The workflow was validated in the Eclipse® treatment planning system and delivered on a ProBeam 360° system.

For weights in the range 0-5, mean absolute errors were below 0.8 for the prostate and brain models (15.9% and 48.1% of all weights, respectively) and below 1.7 for the lung model (31.2%). Mean relative errors were below 10% for the prostate model (5-65, 83.7%), 20% for the brain model (5-65, 51.7%), and 40% for the lung model (5-110, 68.6%); the remaining weights lay above these ranges and accounted for <0.5% of all weights. All delivered plans met the clinical QA acceptance criteria.

Conclusion

The proposed framework demonstrates the technical feasibility of generating IMPT spot weights with deep learning and implementing them on a clinical delivery system. Further improvement is needed for heterogeneous sites such as the lung.

title: Uncertainty quantification for detecting out-of-distribution cases in deep learning segmentation of head and neck organs of interest.
abstract: Purpose Quality assurance (QA) of auto-segmentations is necessary for safe clinical deployment. Deep learning models are optimised for data similar to their training set, but reliability drops with out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs. This study evaluates whether uncertainty quantification (UQ) can detect OOD inputs arising from distribution shift in head and neck organ of interest (OOI) auto-segmentation. Materials and methods Monte Carlo dropout-based uncertainty scores and geometric accuracy of nnU-Net models were evaluated in two experiments. First, as a proof-of-concept, we assessed whether uncertainty scores detect metal artefact (N = 10) from non-artefact cases (N = 10) on a baseline model (mixed training data, N = 620) and a no-metal model (artefact-free training data, N = 620). Second, in a clinically realistic experiment, we split a fine-tuning dataset by uncertainty score to obtain a narrow model (low-uncertainty cases, N = 21) and a broad model (high-uncertainty cases, N = 21). A held-out test set (N = 76) evaluated whether segmentation accuracy differed between uncertainty categories. Results Both experiments showed that uncertainty scores reflect the learned training distribution. In the supervised experiment, the no-metal model demonstrated greater uncertainty score separation between artefact and non-artefact cases (1.1 × 10 5 vs 0.6 × 10 5 ) than the baseline model (1.1 × 10 5 vs 0.8 × 10 5 ). In the unsupervised experiment, the narrow model performed significantly better on certain than uncertain cases (p = 0.04), while no difference was seen for the broad model (p = 0.34), which did include these cases in training. Conclusions Uncertainty quantification can detect distribution shifts in radiotherapy auto-segmentation. This could support automated QA workflows by identifying in-distribution cases and enabling the application of specialised models.

title: Imaging And Outcomes In The Treatment Of Sacral Dural Arteriovenous Fistulas.
abstract: Objective Spinal dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs) in the sacral region are extremely rare and their intradural retrograde draining system has not been investigated in detail. The aim of this study was to characterize the venous drainage patterns of sacral DAVFs based on our clinical experience in treating patients with this condition. Methods We retrospectively reviewed the clinical data of patients with sacral DAVFs treated at our institution from January 2016 to January 2024. Preoperative spinal angiography was used to evaluate the positional relationship between the shunt point of sacral DAVF and the vertebral midline. We proposed that if the location of the shunt point was located on the midline, the draining vein would be the filum terminale vein (FTV); if the shunt point was located off the midline, the draining vein would be the radiculomedullary vein (RMV). Results A total of 17 sacral DAVFs patients treated with direct surgery were included in this study. All patients presented with lower extremity weakness and numbness. Sphincter dysfunction was present in 15 patients (88.2%). The mean interval from symptom onset to diagnosis was 14.1 months (range 1-96 months). Preoperative magnetic resonance imaging(MRI) detected T2 hyperintensity at the level of the conus medullaris and intradural flow voids in all patients. Spinal angiography confirmed the diagnosis of sacral DAVF in all cases, and complete fistula occlusion was achieved with surgical ligation in all patients. Intraoperatively, 4 patients with the midline location of the shunt point were confirmed to have FTV as the draining vein, while the other 13 patients with off-midline shunt point were confirmed to have RMV as the draining vein. The intraoperative findings were completely consistent with the preoperative assessment of the draining veins based on the location of the shunt point. Conclusions The draining veins of sacral DAVFs are not always the FTVs, in fact, most sacral DAVFs drain via the RMV. With our simple imaging-based method, the two different types of draining veins in sacral DAVFs can be preliminarily identified before surgery.

We proposed that if the location of the shunt point was located on the midline, the draining vein would be the filum terminale vein (FTV); if the shunt point was located off the midline, the draining vein would be the radiculomedullary vein (RMV).

A total of 17 sacral DAVFs patients treated with direct surgery were included in this study. All patients presented with lower extremity weakness and numbness. title: Degenerative cervical myelopathy: early detection and the potential for preventing disability.
abstract: Degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM), the most common non-traumatic spinal cord injury, is a prevalent, progressive, and highly disabling neurological disease, causing heterogeneous impairment ranging from sensory loss and impaired hand dexterity to gait, balance, and autonomic dysfunction. Disability often persists despite surgical decompression, and untreated disease can progress to irreversible neurological injury, including tetraplegia. Current clinical management is largely reactive, with diagnosis and intervention typically only after neurological deterioration has become clinically apparent and radiographic evidence of cervical myelopathy is established. Advances in multimodal diagnostics over the past 5 years are now enabling the detection of subtle spinal cord injury, biological disease activity, and subclinical neurodegeneration before overt clinical disability. Quantitative spinal cord MRI, advanced neurophysiological assessments, dynamic biomechanical metrics, and sensitive functional testing provide complementary tools for early detection, risk stratification, and prognostication. Together, these approaches are redefining DCM as a disease that should be managed proactively. Evidence supports decompressive surgery in patients with moderate-to-severe disease, whereas in milder disease or in spinal stenosis that might develop into DCM, the management of patients should be interdisciplinary, with active surveillance to detect early deterioration or decompressive surgery in selected cases. Improved prediction of disease trajectories and clearer evidence on long-term outcomes could enable selective earlier intervention and help to prevent neurological disability.

title: Pulmonary nodules: classification, biomarkers, signaling pathways, diseases, early diagnosis and management.
abstract: Pulmonary nodules are increasingly detected by thoracic imaging and low-dose computed tomography-based lung cancer screening, but most are benign, transient, or indolent. Clinically, the key task is to distinguish nodules that require timely cancer-directed evaluation from those that can be safely observed. This review summarizes the classification, disease spectrum, risk assessment, early diagnosis, biomarkers, signaling mechanisms, translational models, and management of pulmonary nodules. We first distinguish imaging phenotypes and disease entities, then differentiate the individual-level models used to select candidates for lung cancer screening from the nodule-level models and structured reporting systems used after nodule detection. Low-dose computed tomography remains the foundation of screening and surveillance approaches, whereas magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), positron emission tomography combined with computed tomography, contrast-enhanced computed tomography, nonsurgical biopsy, surgical diagnosis, and local therapies play more selective roles depending on the probability of malignancy and patient fitness. Noninvasive biomarkers, including circulating cellular, nucleic acid, methylation, protein, autoantibody, extracellular vesicle, and metabolic analytes, are most likely to serve as adjuncts to imaging and clinical risk assessment rather than as stand-alone diagnostic tests. Artificial intelligence may support detection, workflow efficiency, malignancy risk reclassification, invasiveness assessment, and multimodal integration, but its value depends on external validation, calibration, implementation, and prospective evidence of management benefit. Mechanistic studies of adenocarcinoma spectrum subsolid nodules have implicated the involvement of early oncogenic signaling, genomic instability, immune escape, stromal and vascular remodeling, and adaptive survival pathways. Translational models can support mechanistic and procedural research, but do not replicate real-world nodule management in patients. Overall, care for pulmonary nodules should be risk-adapted, longitudinal, multidisciplinary, and patient-centered.

title: AEGIS: an operational infrastructure for post-market governance of adaptive medical AI under US and EU regulatory frameworks.
abstract: Medical AI requires governance preserving safety during continuous improvement. FDA Predetermined Change Control Plans (PCCP) and EU post-market surveillance address iterative updates but lack operational tooling. We present AEGIS, an internal governance and post-market-monitoring infrastructure designed to support the documentation of predetermined governance pathways for PCCP and Medical Devices Regulation alignment. AEGIS comprises dataset assimilation and retraining, model monitoring, and conditional decision-making modules. It utilizes a four-category taxonomy (APPROVE, CONDITIONAL APPROVAL, CLINICAL REVIEW, REJECT) and an independent ALARM signal. Instantiating AEGIS for sepsis prediction (PhysioNet) and brain-tumor segmentation (BraTS) exercised all decision categories, successfully routing failures to the critical REJECT + ALARM state (no deployable model; released model at risk). On real cross-site data, drift detection ROC-AUC rose from 0.82 to 1.00, reliably triggering near 500-patient batches with zero false alarms. This proof-of-concept utilizes illustrative clinical models; drift scoring quantifies covariate shift only, leaving concept drift for future work.

title: Recent advances in spectral CT contrast agents for gastrointestinal tract imaging.
abstract: Computed tomography (CT) represents one of the most widely utilized and clinically effective imaging techniques for gastrointestinal diseases. Specifically, spectral CT, as an advanced evolution of conventional CT, has significantly improved diagnostic accuracy. The creation of high-performance and biocompatible contrast agents is essential for achieving superior visualization of the gastrointestinal tract and facilitating accurate disease identification. Recent studies reveal that small molecule- and nanoparticle-based contrast agents with high atomic number elements demonstrate significant promise in gastrointestinal diagnostics via spectral CT imaging. Therefore, this review systematically discusses the synthesis, characteristics and advantages of small molecule- and nanoparticle-based contrast agents, with emphasis on their utility in gastrointestinal imaging, disease diagnosis, and therapeutic interventions. Furthermore, the limitations and future directions of current contrast agents are also evaluated, offering a foundation for the design of novel gastrointestinal spectral CT contrast agents.

title: A homologous cell membrane-camouflaged iridium-doped carbon dot nanozyme for multimodal imaging-guided radiosensitization.
abstract: Radiotherapy (RT) is a mainstay of cancer treatment, yet its efficacy is limited by tumor hypoxia, elevated glutathione (GSH) levels, and a lack of tumor-specific radiosensitizers. Herein, we synthesized iridium-doped carbon dots (Ir-CDs) and further camouflaged them with 4T1 cancer cell membranes to construct a biomimetic nanoplatform (Ir-CDs@CM) integrating homologous targeting, multimodal imaging, and nanozyme-mediated properties for enhanced radiosensitization. The synthesized Ir-CDs exhibited a uniform size of ∼2.25 nm and good water dispersibility. After encapsulation with 4T1 cell membranes, Ir-CDs@CM showed an average hydrodynamic diameter of ∼181.9 nm and a zeta potential of -17.0 mV, along with excellent colloidal stability, low cytotoxicity, favorable biocompatibility, and homologous targeting capability. Functionally, Ir-CDs@CM enabled dual-mode fluorescence (FL) and computed tomography (CT) imaging. Moreover, Ir-CDs displayed three nanozyme activities: GSH-depletion activity (47.13% GSH depletion), catalase-like activity (O 2 generation up to 11.9 mg L -1 ), and peroxidase-like activity (a 5.17-fold increase in reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation under X-ray irradiation). This nanozyme-mediated oxygen evolution and ROS generation reduced 4T1 cell viability from 83% to 45.69% under 6 Gy irradiation. In vivo , the nanoplatform achieved excellent tumor accumulation and therapeutic efficacy in subcutaneous tumor-bearing mice, suppressing tumor growth within 14 days. Body weight fluctuations remained below 5% with no hepatorenal toxicity or tissue damage, confirming excellent biosafety. This strategy integrates membrane camouflage with iridium-based nanozyme technology for targeted imaging, microenvironment modulation, and radiosensitization, opening new avenues for integrated tumor therapy and diagnosis.

title: US/ROS-responsive ALN-modified polymer nanoparticles enhance the efficacy of infiltration anesthesia through improved bone targeting and permeation.
abstract: Complex maxillofacial bone anatomy compromises the efficacy of local anesthetics. This study develops an ultrasound (US)/reactive oxygen species (ROS) cascade-responsive polylactic-coglycolic acid (PLGA) nanoparticle system for enhanced dental infiltration anesthesia and perioperative pain management. The nanoparticles, which were surface-modified with alendronate (ALN) via an ROS-cleavable thioketal (TK) linker and coloaded with bupivacaine (BUPI) and perfluorohexane (PFH), enabled enhanced bone targeting and penetration. Under US stimulation, PFH undergoes a liquid-gas phase transition, generating ROS that cleave TK linkers, switching the system from a "bone-targeting" to a "bone-penetration" state. This cascade mechanism facilitates deep tissue penetration of local anesthetics for enhanced anesthesia while enabling a dual-phase release profile: rapid US-triggered BUPI release for intraoperative analgesia and sustained diffusion for postoperative pain management. In rat models of tooth extraction and pulp injury, the system demonstrated superior efficacy over conventional BUPI, significantly increasing drug concentrations in the mandibular bone and improving pain-related outcomes. Biocompatibility was confirmed via histology and serum biomarkers. By overcoming maxillofacial bone barriers and enabling responsive, biphasic drug release, this platform represents a promising strategy to address the limitations of current local anesthetics in dentistry, reducing local anesthesia failure rates and improving perioperative pain control.

title: Nanomedicines for prostate cancer therapy: stimuli-responsive design and disease-specific applications.
abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) remains a major malignancy among men and is clinically complicated by biological heterogeneity, treatment resistance and frequent bone metastasis. Current therapeutic strategies, including radical local treatment, androgen deprivation therapy, androgen receptor (AR) pathway inhibitors, chemotherapy and radioligand therapy, have improved disease control, but their efficacy is often limited by systemic toxicity, functional burden and insufficient tumour selectivity. Chemistry-enabled nanomedicines offer a versatile route to improve drug solubility, circulation, tumour accumulation and controlled therapeutic activation. In this review, we summarise recent advances in nanomedicines for PCa therapy with an emphasis on two closely related aspects: stimuli-responsive design and disease-specific applications. First, endogenous stimuli-responsive drug delivery systems are discussed, including platforms activated by acidic pH, hypoxia, redox imbalance and aberrant enzyme activity. Exogenous systems regulated by light, ultrasound and magnetic fields are then reviewed, with attention to how carrier architecture, responsive linkers, surface transformation and externally triggered activation influence payload release and therapeutic output. Second, PCa-specific nanoplatforms are highlighted, focusing on prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-directed delivery, AR axis- and castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC)-oriented intervention, and bone metastasis-adapted design. Nanomedicine-enabled combinations with immunotherapy or radiotherapy are also considered. Finally, we discuss key challenges related to tumour delivery efficiency, structural complexity, manufacturing reproducibility, biosafety and patient stratification. Overall, this review highlights how rational chemical design can be integrated with prostate cancer biology to develop more precise and clinically translatable nanotherapy strategies.

title: Melanin-like nanoparticles for nanomedicine and drug delivery.
abstract: Melanin plays important roles in coloration and photoprotection in living organisms. Because of its intrinsic biocompatibility, melanin and its biomimetic replicates find important applications in nanomedicine. Thanks to their unique optical and electronic properties, melanin-based materials could be used for both diagnostics and therapeutics. Modes of detection include photoacoustic imaging (PAI) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Therapeutic activities include photothermal therapy (PTT), antioxidant (AOX) therapy, and drug delivery. In this review paper, we summarize and discuss the most recent applications of melanin-like nanoparticles (NPs) as multifunctional agents in nanomedicine and drug delivery. Although most of these applications involve the most popular biomimetic form of melanin, polydopamine (PDA, resulting from the oxidative polymerization of dopamine), in the last part of the review, we show that alternative forms of melanin are becoming more and more important for nanomedicine.

title: An RGD peptide actively targeting nanoprobe with enhanced tumor accumulation for complementary magnetic resonance imaging/NIR-II fluorescence imaging.
abstract: Accurate visualization of tumor lesions with high contrast and well-defined margins remains a major challenge for preoperative evaluation and intraoperative navigation. Conventional single-modal contrast agents mainly rely on passive accumulation, which often suffers from limitations in terms of sensitivity, specificity and tumor uptake, as well as short circulation time in vivo . Therefore, it is necessary to develop high-performance multi-modal nanoprobes with active-targeting ability. Here, we develop an RGD-mediated active-targeted imaging nanoprobe based on lanthanide nanoparticles with a core-shell structure (NaGdF 4 :Er,Yb@NaGdF 4 :Yb,Nd), followed by in situ growth of a mesoporous SiO 2 shell and surface functionalization with DSPE-PEG 2000 -RGD to form the nanoprobe (abbreviated as DSR) for achieving molecular targeting of integrin αvβ 3 on tumor vascular endothelial cells. Under 808 nm excitation, DSR exhibits intense near-infrared IIb (NIR-IIb) emission at 1525 nm, markedly improving the contrast and margin delineation of in vivo tumor imaging. Importantly, the presence of Gd 3+ further endows the nanoprobe with T 1 -weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast, providing complementary anatomical information for tumor localization. With good biocompatibility, DSR can be used for actively targeted NIR-II fluorescence/ T 1 -MRI dual-modal imaging of breast cancer, providing a promising tool for image-guided surgery.

title: Clinical Interpretation and Structured Reporting of Velopharyngeal Magnetic Resonance Imaging: A Framework for Multidisciplinary Decision Making.
abstract: Purpose Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) enables direct visualization of the velopharyngeal (VP) mechanism, including the soft palate, pharyngeal walls, adenoid tissue, and levator veli palatini (LVP) musculature. As VP MRI becomes more integrated into multidisciplinary craniofacial care, speech-language pathologists (SLPs) are increasingly involved in image interpretation. However, structured guidance for translating MRI findings into clinically relevant multidisciplinary decision making remains limited. This study presents a clinically oriented framework for interpretation of VP MRI and introduces a structured reporting approach to support consistent documentation and interdisciplinary communication. Method A literature-informed, consensus-based framework for interpreting VP MRI was developed. Scoping review first identified MRI-derived anatomic variables relevant to VP function. These variables were organized into interpretive domains through multidisciplinary discussion among SLPs, surgeons, and radiologists. The framework was operationalized into structured reporting templates for speech-language pathology and radiology documentation and prospectively piloted in clinical VP MRI cases. Results The resulting framework organizes interpretation across five domains: VP proportional relationships, LVP morphology and function, VP closure dynamics, additional structural contributors, and articulatory context. Structured templates integrate quantitative measurements, qualitative observations, and clinical synthesis. The framework was successfully applied across pilot cases, supporting consistent interpretation and documentation. Conclusion This framework provides clinicians with a practical method for integrating VP MRI observations with speech assessment to enhance clinical reasoning and inform multidisciplinary treatment planning for individuals with VP dysfunction. Supplemental material https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34074555.

However, structured guidance for translating MRI findings into clinically relevant multidisciplinary decision making remains limited. This study presents a clinically oriented framework for interpretation of VP MRI and introduces a structured reporting approach to support consistent documentation and interdisciplinary communication.

Method

A literature-informed, consensus-based framework for interpreting VP MRI was developed. Scoping review first identified MRI-derived anatomic variables relevant to VP function. These variables were organized into interpretive domains through multidisciplinary discussion among SLPs, surgeons, and radiologists. title: Impact of CT-based posterior malleolar fracture classifications on clinical outcomes in bimalleolar ankle fractures involving the posterior and lateral malleoli.
abstract: Background The prognostic value of computed tomography (CT)-based posterior malleolar fracture classifications in uniformly treated fractures remains uncertain. Purpose To examine associations of the Haraguchi, Bartoníček/Rammelt, and Mason-Molloy classifications with 1-year functional and early radiographic outcomes. Study design Retrospective cohort study. Methods Fifty-eight patients with posterior malleolar and Weber B lateral malleolar fractures underwent fixation of both malleoli through a posterolateral approach. Outcomes were the 1-year American Orthopedic Foot & Ankle Society (AOFAS) score and Kellgren-Lawrence grade. Classification subgroups were compared using Kruskal-Wallis tests; fragment dimensions were assessed using Spearman correlations. Results Mean AOFAS score was 92.97 ± 5.28 (95% confidence interval [CI], 91.58-94.35); 10 patients (17%) scored 100 and 24 (41%) scored ≥95. Subgroup mean scores were 91.0-93.3 for Haraguchi (p = 0.994), 84.0-96.5 for Bartoníček/Rammelt (p = 0.130), and 87.0-93.3 for Mason-Molloy (p = 0.836). Kellgren-Lawrence grades did not differ across Haraguchi, Bartoníček/Rammelt, or Mason-Molloy subgroups (p = 0.449, p = 0.277, and p = 0.608, respectively). AOFAS correlations with axial and sagittal fragment lengths were ρ = 0.001 (95% CI, -0.273 to 0.285; p = 0.992) and ρ = 0.049 (95% CI, -0.242 to 0.342; p = 0.717), respectively. Conclusions No significant associations with 1-year outcomes were detected. Small, uneven subgroups and upper-end AOFAS clustering limited precision; potentially meaningful prognostic associations cannot be excluded.

Subgroup mean scores were 91.0-93.3 for Haraguchi (p = 0.994), 84.0-96.5 for Bartoníček/Rammelt (p = 0.130), and 87.0-93.3 for Mason-Molloy (p = 0.836). Kellgren-Lawrence grades did not differ across Haraguchi, Bartoníček/Rammelt, or Mason-Molloy subgroups (p = 0.449, p = 0.277, and p = 0.608, respectively). AOFAS correlations with axial and sagittal fragment lengths were ρ = 0.001 (95% CI, -0.273 to 0.285; p = 0.992) and ρ = 0.049 (95% CI, -0.242 to 0.342; p = 0.717), respectively.

Conclusions

No significant associations with 1-year outcomes were detected. Small, uneven subgroups and upper-end AOFAS clustering limited precision; potentially meaningful prognostic associations cannot be excluded.

title: A Comprehensive Approach to Flexion-Varus Tibial Plateau Fractures: Principles of Systematic Management.
abstract: Abstract Tibial plateau fractures (TPFs) are complex intra-articular injuries frequently accompanied by significant soft tissue injury. Existing medical literature has shown that TPFs resulting from a flexion-varus injury mechanism, affecting the posteromedial column primarily, are associated with worse clinical outcome scores and a higher risk of conversion to total knee arthroplasty. This narrative review aims to explain why this specific subgroup has a poorer prognosis compared with other TPFs subtypes. Four key factors are examined in this review: fracture morphology, biomechanics, soft tissue involvement, and surgical management. The complex fracture morphology of flexion-varus TPFs can be most accurately assessed using three-dimensional computed tomography-based reconstructions. The mechanism of injury helps to better understand fracture morphology and potential soft tissue injury. Soft tissue injuries are frequent in these type of fractures, such as anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) avulsion fracture, lateral meniscus tears, and entrapment. These three elements are important for better understanding TPFs and adequately planning surgical strategy. The severity of the fracture and the involvement of the posterolateral depression complicate surgical treatment. Visualization of the posteromedial compartment is essential but remains challenging. Anatomical reduction and stable fixation of the posteromedial and posterolaterocentral tibial plateau, with consideration of any meniscal injury, should be performed with care. An ACL avulsion fracture should ideally be fixed. Although preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides valuable information about the soft tissue involved, this examination is not yet routinely performed. Given the high incidence of ACL and (lateral) meniscal injury, an MRI is highly recommended.

title: [Molecular-Based Diagnostics and Therapy of Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer (mHSPC)].
abstract: Abstract Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) represents a biologically and clinically heterogeneous disease entity. While traditional clinical parameters such as metastatic burden and timing of metastasis remain prognostically relevant, molecular biomarkers are increasingly gaining importance for individualized treatment planning. Genetic alterations in tumor suppressor genes and DNA repair pathways, particularly BRCA, PTEN, and TP53 aberrations, are associated with more aggressive disease courses and poorer prognosis. At the same time, these molecular alterations provide novel therapeutic opportunities, including the use of PARP inhibitors and AKT inhibitors.In addition to genetic alterations, transcriptomic characteristics also play an important role. In particular, androgen receptor (AR) pathway activity influences prognosis and treatment response. Low AR activity and reduced PSMA expression have been associated with reduced sensitivity to hormonal therapies and increased biological heterogeneity. Conversely, high PSMA expression appears to correlate with improved responses to androgen deprivation therapy as well as PSMA-targeted radioligand therapies.Advanced imaging modalities such as PSMA PET imaging further contribute to a refined understanding of metastatic disease biology and increasingly challenge traditional disease classifications. Moreover, biomarkers including PSA nadir or circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) may help identify progression patterns and guide future treatment intensification or de-escalation strategies.Overall, current evidence suggests that integrating genetic, transcriptomic, and imaging biomarkers may substantially improve the biological characterization of mHSPC. In the future, these approaches could enable a more accurate prognostic stratification and support the development of personalized therapeutic concepts.

title: Clinical management and multimodal imaging features of brucellar mastitis mimicking metastatic breast carcinoma: a rare case report and literature review.
abstract: Brucella mastitis represents a rare infectious disease that is frequently misdiagnosed as metastatic breast carcinoma, particularly when older women present with systemic manifestations. Here, we report a 60-year-old woman presenting with a neck pain and left upper extremity numbness. Initial contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (CEMR) and 18 F -FDG PET-CT highly suggested breast malignancy with osseous metastasis, while contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) provided critical microvascular perfusion insights favoring an inflammatory process. The diagnosis was ultimately confirmed via blood culture and pathological examination. The patient was successfully treated with targeted antimicrobial treatment. This case offers important insights into the multimodal imaging differentiation of atypical breast lesions and emphasizes the diagnostic challenges of Brucella mastitis accompanied by systemic osteoarticular involvement.

title: CT image-based evaluation of phantom-derived DLP-to-effective dose conversion factors for adult abdomen-pelvis CT.
abstract: Effective dose is used in computed tomography (CT) as a population-level quantity for radiation protection, dose monitoring, and clinical studies. It is commonly estimated by multiplying scanner-reported dose-length product (DLP) by a conversion coefficient, or k -factor, because organ doses are not available from routine examinations. Most CT k -factors were derived from computational human phantoms, but phantom-derived estimates have not been systematically compared with effective doses calculated directly from CT images across adults with diverse body habitus. We calculated k -factors using a set of adult abdominal CT images combined with deep learning-based automatic organ segmentation and Monte Carlo dose calculation methods and compared them with those calculated from two phantom-derived k -factor approaches: the fixed AAPM TG23 coefficient and body size-dependent k -factors calculated using National Cancer Institute dosimetry system for CT (NCICT). Abdomen-pelvis CT images from 38 adults (18 females, 20 males) spanning water-equivalent diameter (WED) values of 21-41 cm were segmented using TotalSegmentator and an in-house gonad model, converted into voxelised anatomical models, and coupled with a validated CT scanner Monte Carlo model. CT image-based k -factors were calculated as effective dose divided by DLP and evaluated as functions of WED and sex. Image-based k -factors decreased with increasing WED for both sexes, and female values were higher than male values at comparable WED. Over the overlapping WED range, NCICT-based k -factors showed good agreement with CT-based values with the same decreasing trend. The fixed TG23 coefficient introduced systematic bias at smaller and larger body sizes. However, the selected NCICT adult phantoms did not cover the lower-WED end of the CT cohort. These findings support the performance of phantom-based effective dose calculations and indicate the need to extend phantom libraries while continuing CT image-based evaluation across pediatric CT and broader imaging protocols.

title: RibXcar: Safety Fundamentals and Surgical Protocol for Controlled Costal Osteotomy in Body Contouring Surgery: A Prospective Study of 100 Patients.
abstract: Background Aesthetic body contouring surgery has incorporated costal modification techniques to improve waist definition. The lack of standardized protocols and prospective safety data has generated controversy. The RibXcar technique proposes a controlled monocortical costal osteotomy as an alternative to rib resection; however, no prospective studies have comprehensively evaluated its safety profile. Objectives To describe a standardized surgical protocol for the RibXcar technique and prospectively evaluate its safety, efficacy, impact on pulmonary function, postoperative pain, and patient satisfaction. Methods A prospective study of 100 consecutive patients who underwent RibXcar alone (n=80) or combined with body liposuction (n=20). A 10-step protocol was described, and outcomes were evaluated: complications, pulmonary function (spirometry), waist diameter, costal angulation (ultrasound), pain (VAS), and satisfaction (Body-Q) preoperatively and at 6 months. Results The overall minor complication rate was 8%, with no cases of pneumothorax or hemothorax. Pulmonary function showed no significant changes at 6 months in either group. Waist diameter reduction was 5.0 cm (IQR: 3.75-7.0) in the RibXcar group and 10.50 ± 1.73 cm in the combined group (P < .001). Costal angulation decreased significantly in all evaluated ribs (P < .0001). Body-Q scores improved significantly (P < .00001), and pain resolved by 6 months. Conclusions The results of this series suggest that RibXcar, when performed under a standardized protocol, may constitute a safe and effective alternative for aesthetic rib remodeling in selected patients. The preservation of pulmonary function and the low complication rate observed would support its implementation in advanced body contouring surgery.

title: XCREST II: The X-factor in Iliac Crest Remodeling for Advanced Waist-to-hip Definition.
abstract: Background Modern body contouring has evolved toward structural reshaping, with the waist-hip-gluteal unit as a key determinant of body contour aesthetics. The iliac crest is a critical landmark for lower waist contour. Objectives To evaluate the aesthetic outcomes, safety, and anatomical contribution of XCREST II, a combined bony and myofascial technique for lower waist contouring. Methods A multicenter retrospective cohort study included 480 patients who underwent XCREST II between 2024 and 2026. Patients were categorized into four groups: XCREST II alone (n = 180), XCREST II + gluteal fat grafting (n = 84), XCREST II + RibXcar (n = 132), and XCREST II + RibXcar + gluteal fat grafting (n = 84). All underwent ultrasound-guided iliac crest remodeling with partial gluteus medius detachment. Anthropometric and BODY-Q outcomes were assessed preoperatively and at 12 months. Results Four hundred eighty patients were included. Baseline characteristics were comparable, except for longer operative time in combined procedures (p < 0.001). At 12 months, all anthropometric measures improved significantly from baseline across groups (p < 0.001), without intergroup differences. Complications were low; prolonged postoperative pain and iliac crest pain were more frequent in groups including RibXCar (p = 0.020 and p = 0.017, respectively), without chronic pain. BODY-Q scores improved significantly across all domains (p < 0.001), differing only in body image (p = 0.019) and scar assessment (p < 0.001). Conclusions XCREST II, a refinement of XCREST incorporating partial gluteus medius detachment, demonstrated favorable 12-month waist contour improvement and high patient satisfaction, with a low complication rate. Outcomes were consistent across subgroups.

title: Complex relationship between iron status and outcomes of STEMI: hypothesis-generating study.
abstract: Aims Iron deficiency (ID) is common amongst patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Its impact on outcomes remains contested. Previous studies reported favourable or adverse impacts depending on outcome measures, sampling timepoints, ID definition and follow-up duration. This study systematically characterises the prognostic impact of iron status on short-term, mid-term and long-term outcomes, and evaluates the effect of sampling timepoint and ID definition on these prognostic relationships. Methods & results We performed an observational cohort study in patients with acute STEMI (n = 167) and no prior heart failure (HF). Iron markers were sampled at presentation, and successive timepoints thereafter. Cardiac Magnetic Resonance was performed at 2 days and 6 months. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), consisting of new-onset HF, recurrent MI or cardiac death were recorded over 4.5 years. Mechanisms were evaluated in a preclinical model of MI.ID was common at presentation, affecting between 44.9% and 67%, depending on ID definition. Tsat <20%, serum iron<13μM, or European Society of Cardiology's definition, but not ferritin<100μg/L, independently predicted lower risk of MACE. Lower Tsat at presentation predicted attenuated infarct and non-infarct T1, and smaller left ventricular volumes at 2 days. This prognostic effect was weakened by delayed sampling. Lower Tsat and serum iron in the post-acute timepoints, but not at presentation, predicted lower myocardial salvage at 6 months. In mice, MI triggered an acute myocardial labile iron storm and early LV remodelling, progressing to HF. Baseline ID and acute iron chelation averted these effects. Conclusions This study gives rise to the hypothesis that ID at presentation with STEMI improves long-term outcomes by attenuating myocardial injury. It reconciles previous conflicting reports by revealing the confounding effects of delayed sampling, and non-interchangeability of different ID definitions. It suggests iron chelation in the acute stage, followed by post-acute iron repletion might improve long-term outcomes.

Lower Tsat at presentation predicted attenuated infarct and non-infarct T1, and smaller left ventricular volumes at 2 days. This prognostic effect was weakened by delayed sampling. Lower Tsat and serum iron in the post-acute timepoints, but not at presentation, predicted lower myocardial salvage at 6 months. In mice, MI triggered an acute myocardial labile iron storm and early LV remodelling, progressing to HF. Baseline ID and acute iron chelation averted these effects.

Conclusions

This study gives rise to the hypothesis that ID at presentation with STEMI improves long-term outcomes by attenuating myocardial injury. It reconciles previous conflicting reports by revealing the confounding effects of delayed sampling, and non-interchangeability of different ID definitions. It suggests iron chelation in the acute stage, followed by post-acute iron repletion might improve long-term outcomes.

title: Changes In body composition and subsequent risk of relapse In childhood hodgkin lymphoma.
abstract: Background Whether changes in body composition (skeletal muscle and adipose tissue, measured using computed tomography [CT] scans) are associated with relapse in children with Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) remains unknown. Methods We examined changes in body composition (skeletal muscle area [SMA] and total adipose tissue [TAT] area) of children with intermediate- and high-risk HL enrolled on Children's Oncology Group trials AHOD0031 and AHOD0831 using commercially available software from pre-treatment to after two cycles of chemotherapy. SMA or TAT values exceeding the median increase were classified as excessive gain, and those exceeding the median decline were classified as excessive loss in SMA or TAT. Proportional sub-distribution hazard regression models examined the association between change in body composition and relapse from end of cycle 2 treating non-relapse-related death as competing risk and adjusting for prognosticators including baseline SMA and TAT. Results Among the 951 children included in this analysis, the median age at diagnosis was 15.2y, 53.8% were male and 63.5% were non-Hispanic White. Excessive gain in TAT (observed in 36.2%) was associated with a 1.73-fold greater adjusted hazard of relapse (95% confidence interval [CI]=1.08-2.77, P=0.02) among children with negative PET2, but not among those with positive PET2 (hazard ratio [HR]=0.90, 95%CI=0.51-1.57, P=0.70) after adjusting for prognosticators. Excessive change in SMA was not associated with relapse. Conclusions This candidate biomarker is associated with an increased risk of relapse and presents a need to understand the underlying mechanisms for this association.

title: AI in Neuro-Oncology: An Overarching Review.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across neuro-oncology domains to analyze complex, high-dimensional, multimodal data. Despite major advances in the biological understanding and classification of CNS tumors, clinical outcomes for many of them remain poor, reflecting intra- and inter-tumor heterogeneity and limitations of conventional reductionist approaches. AI offers a paradigm shift to capture this heterogeneity and provide quantitative, reproducible diagnostic, predictive, and prognostic insights. This article describes a joint effort across the Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology (RANO) working groups to provide an overarching review of the AI use across six key domains of neuro-oncology: neuroimaging, neuropathology, laboratory medicine, neurosurgery, drug discovery, and clinical trials. Applications closest to clinical use include imaging segmentation and quantification, AI-assisted image reconstruction, DNA methylation-based classification, and workflow optimization. Radiogenomics, WSI-based molecular prediction, AI-guided surgical targeting, liquid biopsy interpretation, AI-guided drug discovery, digital twins, and in silico trials remain promising but require stronger prospective validation. Key challenges include limited availability of large diverse datasets, variability in data acquisition and reference standards, and limited external validation. This review provides a unifying framework for understanding the role of AI across neuro-oncology and highlights key considerations for its responsible implementation, emphasizing standardization, reproducibility, multi-institutional validation, and human oversight.

title: Preoperative ultrasound in pediatric supracondylar fracture-related nerve injuries: intraoperative correlation in a tertiary referral retrospective case series.
abstract: Nerve palsy is a recognized complication of paediatric supracondylar humeral fractures. Most injuries recover spontaneously, a subset require surgical exploration, and identifying those who may benefit from intervention remains challenging. High-resolution ultrasound has emerged as a potential adjunct for assessing nerve injury, although its utility in this setting remains incompletely defined. A retrospective case series was conducted at a tertiary peripheral nerve injury center. Children less than 16 years with persistent supracondylar fracture-related nerve palsy who underwent preoperative ultrasound and surgical exploration between 2018 and 2024 were included. Ultrasound findings were categorized as structural abnormality, compression/tethering, neuroma/swelling, or entrapment and were compared with intraoperative findings. Analysis was descriptive, focusing on ultrasound detection of nerve abnormality and concordance with surgical findings. Twenty-two patients were included (mean age: 7 years). All had surgically confirmed nerve pathology. Ultrasound demonstrated nerve abnormality in 21 out of 22 cases (95%). Compression/tethering was the most common finding (18/22), followed by structural abnormality (14/22), neuroma/swelling (7/22), and entrapment (2/22). Intraoperatively, structural abnormalities were identified in 17 cases, compression/tethering in 21, neuroma in 3, and entrapment in 4. Ultrasound frequently identified nerve abnormality but demonstrated variable concordance with intraoperative findings, including overestimation of neuroma (7 vs. 3 cases) and under-detection of entrapment (2 vs. 4 cases). Preoperative ultrasound frequently demonstrated abnormal nerve features in children with persistent palsy following supracondylar humeral fracture. However, its limited concordance in characterizing specific pathology restricts its role as a standalone decision-making tool. Ultrasound findings should be interpreted alongside clinical assessment when considering surgical exploration.

title: Subperiosteal hematoma of the ilium in adolescent athletes with acute groin pain: clinical and MRI features of a radiograph-occult injury pattern.
abstract: Subperiosteal hematoma of the ilium is an uncommon MRI finding in young athletes with acute groin pain and is frequently occult on plain radiographs. This study aimed to characterize its clinical presentation, MRI findings, associated injuries, and return-to-sport outcomes. This retrospective single-center case series included athletes aged ≤22 years who underwent MRI for acute sports-related groin pain with negative or inconclusive radiographs between 2017 and 2025. Patients meeting predefined MRI criteria for subperiosteal hematoma of the ilium were identified, and clinical, imaging, and outcome data were analyzed descriptively. Twenty of 91 patients (22.0%) met the MRI criteria. Their mean age was 13.9 ± 1.5 years, 19 (95%) were male, and 18 (90%) had open physes. Periosteal elevation was present in all patients, and 19 (95%) demonstrated a predominantly subperiosteal fluid collection, most commonly with a lentiform configuration. Associated anterior inferior iliac spine avulsion injury or intramuscular iliacus injury was identified in 10 patients (50%). All patients were managed nonoperatively and returned to unrestricted sports participation after progressive rehabilitation at a mean of 4.5 ± 2.2 weeks. Subperiosteal hematoma of the ilium is a reproducible MRI finding in predominantly skeletally immature athletes with acute sports-related groin pain and negative or inconclusive radiographs. Recognition of periosteal elevation with a predominantly subperiosteal fluid collection may facilitate diagnosis of this radiograph-occult injury pattern. Although the underlying injury mechanism remains hypothetical, prospective studies are needed to clarify its clinical significance.

title: Relationship between extent of jeopardized myocardium derived from myocardial viability study to post-myocardial infarction outcome.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to assess the relationship between the extent of jeopardized myocardium, quantified using cardiac viability imaging, and clinical outcomes in patients after myocardial infarction. By utilizing rest myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) and cardiac 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) analyzed with Emory Cardiac Toolbox software (ECTb), the study aimed to determine how quantitative viability parameters correlate with left ventricular functional recovery and post-myocardial infarction outcomes, and to assess their utility in guiding clinical decision-making. Methods This prospective study included 85 patients who underwent 2-day rest MPI followed by cardiac FDG-PET/CT imaging. Quantitative parameters, including the percentage of jeopardized myocardium, comprising viable, scarred, and total jeopardized myocardial segments, along with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) were obtained using the ECTb platform (version 4.2). The relationship between these quantitative PET parameters and functional myocardial recovery, defined as improvement in ≥5% LVEF as assessed by two-dimensional echocardiography, was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Follow-up was conducted over a period of 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year to assess the association between baseline quantitative imaging parameters and the occurrence of adverse cardiac events. Results The analysis demonstrated that the extent of viable myocardium was a strong predictor of functional recovery (area under the curve, 0.762; P < 0.001), with a cutoff of approximately 17% yielding 76.7% sensitivity, 68.8% specificity, and 71.8% accuracy. Major adverse cardiac events (MACE) occurred in 16% of patients. There was no significant association with imaging parameters, except a nonsignificant trend for scar burden in medically managed patients. Patients undergoing surgical intervention had a significantly greater extent of jeopardized myocardium, underscoring the role of viability imaging in therapeutic decision-making. Conclusion The extent of viable myocardium identified through imaging was strongly correlated with functional recovery, as reflected by improvements in cardiac function on follow-up echocardiography. Although no significant relationship with MACE was seen in the overall cohort, the higher burden of jeopardized myocardium in surgically treated patients underscores the value of viability imaging in guiding revascularization decisions, supporting FDG-PET/CT as a useful tool for post-myocardial infarction risk stratification and management.

abstract: Purpose First, to assess the diagnostic value of fluorine-18-fluorodeoxyglucose PET-computed tomography ([18F]-FDG PET-CT) compared with conventional MRI and/or CT. Second, to audit the clinical indications for referring patients with cervical cancer for [18F]-FDG PET-CT against the 2022 guidelines published by the Royal College of Radiologists and the Royal College of Physicians. Finally, to evaluate the impact of [18F]-FDG PET-CT on management plans. Methods A retrospective cohort study of 49 patients with histologically proven cervical cancer across the Sussex Cancer Network underwent 59 [18F]-FDG PET-CT between 1 November 2020 and 31 October 2022. Scans were compared with the most recent CT and MRI scan conducted within 4 months of the [18F]-FDG PET-CT. Scan indications were categorized as either 'in accordance' or 'outside' the guidelines. Those in accordance fell into one of four groups: staging, response assessment, suspected recurrence, or staging when considering exenterative surgery. A questionnaire investigating the impact of the [18F]-FDG PET-CT on the management plan of each patient was answered by one clinical oncology consultant. Results [18F]-FDG PET-CT identified new metastatic sites in 16/59 (27.1%) scans. The remaining scans were concordant with the CT and MRI. The majority, 57/59 (96.6%), of the scans were performed in accordance with the guidelines. The management plan was changed by 5/59 scans (8.4%), confirmed by 48/59 (81.4%) and was not impacted with 6/59 (10.2%) scans. Conclusion [18F]-FDG PET-CT is superior to conventional imaging and enhances the management plan. Future cohort studies with larger patient numbers involving multicentric studies are needed to fully assess its impact on cervical cancer management and prognosis.

title: EyeGraph: A Multi-granularity Medical Vision-Language Foundation Model with Knowledge Graph Reasoning for Ophthalmic Interpretation.
abstract: The exponential growth of large vision-language models (VLMs) has created significant opportunities for advancing multimodal artificial intelligence in specialized domains such as ophthalmology. However, progress in ophthalmic VLMs remains limited, primarily due to the lack of large-scale, high-quality image-text pairs. Moreover, existing VLMs frequently generate hallucinations, leading to uncertainty and unreliability that are unacceptable in clinical practice. To address the data scarcity issue, we introduce IT-Retinal, a dedicated ophthalmic Vision Question Answering (VQA) dataset that providesmultigranularity tasks and high-quality long-form textual content in image-text pairs. To mitigate hallucinations, we propose EyeGraph, a framework for ophthalmic VLMs that consists of two training stages, targeted pre-training and fine-tuning, and one inference stage that integrates Graph of Thought (GoT) and Think on Graph (ToG) reasoning, referred to as G2T. This design enables EyeGraph to incorporate structured external knowledge, constrain the output space, and produce more clinically consistent results. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EyeGraph achieves state-of-the-art performance across seven clinically relevant benchmarks, spanning disease diagnosis, structural detection and localization, and report generation. Notably, the proposed G2T reasoning module consistently improves the factual consistency and reliability of ophthalmic report generation. All source code, along with an interactive demo, is publicly available at: https://github.com/ZardCAI/EyeGraph.

title: Towards Medical Image Dataset Distillation: A Progressive Trajectory Matching and Dynamic Diversity Enhancing Method.
abstract: Sharing medical image sets is essential yet challenging due to limited resource and strict regulatory, which significantly hinder the development of medical foundation models and the transfer of medical domain knowledge. In this paper, we utilize medical image dataset distillation techniques to enable effective model construction and knowledge transfer without requiring downstream users to directly access the original data. Trajectory matching has become the mainstream distillation technique, yet our empirical findings on medical image datasets reveal two critical phenomena: instability of distillation optimization and redundancy of synthetic images. To investigate these phenomena, we conduct a theoretical analysis from the perspectives of bi-level optimization and neural tangent kernel, and formally define them as two core challenges: trajectory matching drift and intra-class diversity decay, which underscore the need for more stable and diversity-preserving trajectory matching methods. Guided by the analysis results, we propose a novel progressive and diverse dataset distillation (PD$^{3}$) method, which incorporates (1) a progressive trajectory matching paradigm that progressively unrolls the student training trajectory to extend the matching horizon, while adaptively selecting optimal expert matching trajectory to ensure stable and convergent distillation optimization; and (2) a dynamic diversity enhancing module that alleviates the redundancy of synthetic images by enhancing intra-class distribution and breaking redundancy accumulation. To facilitate fair evaluation, we establish a comprehensive medical image dataset distillation benchmark covering diverse medical image modalities. Extensive experiments show that the proposed method achieves an average absolute improvement of 10.20% and a relative gain of 20.09% over prior state-of-the-art methods, highlighting its effectiveness and practical potential.

title: Association Between Local Factors and Implant-Related Complications: A Population-Sampled Cross-Sectional Analysis.
abstract: Aim To investigate the role of local factors and the association with peri-implantitis and peri-implant soft-tissue dehiscence (PISTD). Materials and methods A randomly selected sample of Norwegian patients who underwent implant therapy in 2014 was examined (242 patients; 732 implants). Clinical and radiographic parameters were recorded, including soft-tissue phenotype, mucosal margin mobility, connection type, platform switching, emergence angle, implant location and presence of adjacent teeth. To account for clustering of implants within patients, mixed-effects logistic regression models were applied. Results Mucosal margin mobility, bone-level implants without platform switching, emergence angle > 45°, anterior implant location and daily smoking were identified as significant risk indicators for peri-implantitis. Thin soft-tissue phenotype, mucosal margin mobility, absence of adjacent teeth, peri-implantitis and external connection were detected as significant indicators for PISTD. Peri-implantitis and PISTD were present in 8.7% and 25.0% of implants, respectively. Conclusions Local factors and soft-tissue-related parameters, many modifiable during treatment planning, were associated with peri-implantitis and PISTD. Particular attention should be given to soft-tissue phenotype, connection design, platform switching and prosthetic emergence angle. The relationship between systemic and local risk factors should be further investigated.

title: Experience-based recommendations for the diagnosis and management of early-stage nail unit melanoma.
abstract: Background Nail unit melanoma (NUM) is a distinct form of melanoma that most often arises from the nail matrix. No recommendations as to the management of nail melanoma, particularly of early-stage melanoma (in situ, stage IA, IB), exist. Objectives To provide practical, experience-based recommendations for the diagnosis, differential diagnosis and management of early-stage NUM, developed by an international expert panel. Methods Based on clinical and histopathological experience and an extensive literature search, the authors present recommendations for the management of patients with lesions suspicious for NUM. Results Clinically, most cases present as a longitudinal pigmented band in an adult nail. It represents 1.5-2.5% of all melanomas in Caucasians but up to 50% in Black patients. Considering that the nail unit surface area accounts for less than 1% of the total body surface, the nail matrix can be regarded as a hotspot for melanoma development. Early diagnosis is critical, as treatment at the in situ or minimally invasive stage is associated with high cure rates. While dermoscopy is a useful diagnostic aid, nail matrix biopsy with histopathology remains the gold standard. Laboratory tests and standard imaging studies are not diagnostic; however, they may assist in surgical planning for advanced cases. Complete surgical excision is the treatment of choice. Wide local excision is recommended for early-stage disease, with specific margins (6 mm for standard lesions; 10 mm in the presence of the Hutchinson sign). Amputation is generally reserved for thicker tumours (>1 mm). A 10-year follow-up period is recommended to monitor for potential recurrence. Conclusions Early diagnosis and treatment of nail unit melanoma at the in situ or minimally invasive stage (IA/IB) are associated with high cure rates. In contrast, advanced disease with deep invasion or metastasis carries a poor prognosis-therefore, timely recognition and intervention are essential to optimize outcomes.

title: A Case Report of a Complete Removable Denture Designed to Restore Function in a Patient With Severe Resorption of the Mandibular Alveolar Ridge Using the Neutral Zone and Flange Techniques.
abstract: Edentulous patients with severe mandibular alveolar ridge resorption struggle with denture stability, which often reduces their quality of life due to mucosal pain and food debris retention. When the inferior alveolar canal is extremely close to the alveolar crest, conventional dentures risk causing severe pain and sensory abnormalities by compressing the inferior alveolar nerve. Thus, conventional fabrication methods face clinical limitations. To stabilize a mandibular complete denture in such cases, it is highly effective to record the dynamics of the denture space and fabricate a prosthesis that harmonizes with these perioral muscle movements. A 77-year-old woman presented with frequent stomatitis caused by ill-fitting dentures and severe masticatory dysfunction. Intraoral and radiographic examinations revealed marked resorption of the mandibular alveolar ridge, placing the inferior alveolar canal in extreme proximity to the alveolar crest. The treatment plan involved fabricating a new maxillary partial denture that strictly balanced the support of the remaining teeth. For the mandible, a complete denture was fabricated using the neutral zone and flange techniques to harmonize with surrounding soft tissue movements. This approach enabled functional contouring by leveraging the dynamic pressure of the perioral muscles. Consequently, denture retention and stability improved dramatically, and denture displacement during speech was successfully suppressed. An evaluation of masticatory function confirmed objective functional recovery. This case demonstrates that for patients with severe alveolar ridge resorption and diminished anatomical supporting tissues, determining the functional form of the denture by accounting for soft-tissue dynamics is highly effective in restoring stability and masticatory function.

title: Ovarian Yolk Sac Tumor in a 10-Year-Old Girl Following Metachronous Bilateral Mature Ovarian Teratomas.
abstract: Background Ovarian germ cell tumors are the most common ovarian malignancies in children. Because these patients have a notable risk of developing metachronous bilateral tumors or recurrences, maximizing the preservation of ovarian tissue during initial surgery is critical to protecting future fertility and endocrine function. Objective A previously healthy 8-year-old girl underwent emergency laparotomy for ovarian torsion, resulting the right oophorectomy, with histopathology confirming a mature teratoma. Sixteen months later, a contralateral ovarian mass was detected and treated with ovarian-sparing excision, also diagnosed as a mature teratoma. At age 10 (10 months after the second excision), she was found to have an 8 cm pelvic tumor and elevated α -fetoprotein. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed complex solid and cystic components suggestive of a malignant germ cell tumor, with no metastases on computed tomography/MRI. The mass was removed intact at exploratory laparotomy, yielding a diagnosis of Fédération Internationale de Gynécologie et d'Obstétrique (FIGO) Stage 1A ovarian yolk sac tumor. She was discharged after completing combination chemotherapy. Currently, she is 16 years old and being managed with hormone replacement therapy. Conclusions The presented case highlights a disadvantage of overzealous oophorectomy. Detorsion of the seemingly necrotic ovary followed by second-look surgery could have preserved some ovarian function.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Anomalous Aortic Origin of Right Coronary Artery from the Left Coronary Sinus.
abstract: Introduction Anomalous Aortic Origin of Right Coronary Artery (AAORCA) is a rare congenital anomaly that may be associated with adverse cardiac events, including sudden cardiac death. Surgical correction is commonly recommended in patients with AAORCA. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is a prevalent diagnostic modality, which increases AAORCA detection. However, the clinical significance of incidentally detected AAORCA remains unclear. Methods This non-randomized retrospective analysis included 10,134 patients who underwent CCTA between January 2014 and December 2022, either for suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) or a medical check-up. Three groups were created: patients with normal coronary anatomy (normal), with AAORCA (anomaly), and CAD without AAORCA (CAD). CAD was defined as a percentage diameter stenosis of ≥50% in one or more segments. Cardiac mortality was this study's primary endpoint. Results Normal, anomaly, and CAD group comprised 7592 (74.9%), 66 (0.7%), and 2476 (24.4%) patients, respectively. During a median follow-up of 33.7 months (IQR: 13.2-53.4), Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed no significant difference in the cardiac death occurrence between the normal (15 events, 0.2%) and anomaly groups (0 events, 0%) (log-rank p=0.685). Cox proportional hazards model revealed no difference in mortality in the anomaly group compared with normal group. Conclusions In our cohort, incidentally detected AAORCA in adults did not demonstrate a clearly elevated cardiac death risk relative to CAD during mid-term follow-up. However, given the small number of events, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive rather than confirmatory evidence of a benign natural course, particularly in populations at higher risk of exertional sudden cardiac death.

title: Impact of <sup>18</sup>FDG-Avidity and Immunosuppression on Idiopathic and Genetic Cardiomyopathies.
abstract: Background Myocardial 18 fluorodeoxyglucose ( 18 FDG)-avidity is frequently seen in patients with genetic cardiomyopathy, as well as a growing "idiopathic 18 FDG-avidity" group of genotype-negative patients who do not clearly have cardiac sarcoidosis. The prognostic implications of 18 FDG-avidity in patients with and without genetic cardiomyopathy, and the effects of immunosuppression in the latter, remain uncertain. Methods This multicenter, retrospective study included all patients who were referred for both 18 FDG-PET and cardiomyopathy genetic testing. Patients with acute myocarditis, biopsy-proven sarcoidosis, or extracardiac 18 FDG-avidity were excluded. We investigated heart failure (HF) composite (left ventricular assist device, heart transplant, HF hospitalization, or death) and arrhythmia composite (sustained ventricular arrhythmias [ventricular tachycardia/VF], atrioventricular block, or death) outcomes using survival analysis, including Cox proportional hazards modeling and inverse probability of treatment weighting. Results Among 372 patients, 142 (38%) were 18 FDG-avid. The prevalence of genetic cardiomyopathy among 18 FDG-avid patients (12%) was similar to that of 18 FDG-negative patients (18%; P =0.11). Unadjusted, 18 FDG-avidity was associated with an increased risk of HF composite (hazard ratio, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.04-2.75]; P =0.034) and arrhythmia composite (hazard ratio, 1.63 [95% CI, 1.1-2.4]; P =0.014) outcomes compared with 18 FDG-negative patients. However, these associations were not statistically significant after multivariable adjustment, nor were there significant differences in 18 FDG-associated risks in patients with genetic cardiomyopathy versus genotype-negative patients. After inverse probability of treatment weighting, immunosuppression of 18 FDG-avid patients (n=49) was not associated with a reduction in HF or arrhythmia composite outcomes compared with those who were not immunosuppressed (n=93). Conclusions Myocardial-only 18 FDG-avidity is not significantly associated with HF or arrhythmia risk in patients who do not clearly have cardiac sarcoidosis (including those with genetic cardiomyopathy). Immunosuppression therapy does not seem to modify the disease course, suggesting that not all myocardial 18 FDG uptake reflects clinically significant inflammation.

title: Artificial Intelligence Across the Surgical Research Workflow: A Stage-Specific Framework for Benefits, Failure Modes, and Oversight.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools, particularly large language models (LLMs), have rapidly integrated into surgical and biomedical research, prompting fundamental questions about their appropriate role. This review presents a stage-specific framework mapping each phase of the surgical research workflow (literature review, data analysis, manuscript preparation, and research synthesis) to the role AI plays, the benefits it provides, the failure modes it introduces, and the oversight it requires. Artificial intelligence-powered query systems are designed to speed literature synthesis across thousands of publications. In data analysis, LLMs paired with statistical environments can perform regression modeling and generate auditable code, while specialized architectures support automated image segmentation and histopathology analysis. Each stage's benefits, however, are matched by characteristic failure modes: LLMs are prone to error and hallucination, reproducibility is threatened by model versioning and run-to-run variability, fabricated citations and paper-mill submissions endanger the integrity of the literature, and over-reliance risks eroding trainee competencies in critical appraisal and biostatistical reasoning. Because these failure modes are stage-specific, governance must be stage-specific as well: the framework pairs each risk with a matched oversight mechanism, and these mechanisms translate into practical implementation recommendations for surgical departments, residency programs, research groups, and journals. The integration of AI into surgical scholarship should be viewed as augmentation rather than replacement, supported by standardized disclosure frameworks, AI literacy in graduate medical education, and institutional governance structures that preserve the integrity of surgical research.

title: Limb Body Wall Complex: Report of a Discordant Case in a Monozygotic Twin Pregnancy.
abstract: Limb Body Wall Complex (LBWC) is a rare, severe congenital malformation syndrome characterized by thoracoabdominal wall defects, craniofacial anomalies, and limb and spinal malformations. Its incidence ranges from 0.04 to 3.3 per 10,000 births. We present a case of LBWC diagnosed in a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy at 17 weeks of gestation. The mother was 28-year-old, primigravida, and had no notable medical history. Ultrasound identified abnormal positioning of 1 embryo, suggestive of adherence to the amnion. First-trimester scans revealed increased nuchal translucency and foot malposition in fetus A, while fetus B showed a cystic hygroma along with significant abdominal wall and spinal anomalies. Selective termination of fetus B was performed at 17 weeks but was complicated by the intrauterine demise of both fetuses. Postmortem examination of fetus B confirmed classical LBWC features: abdominopelvic wall defect with evisceration adherent to the placenta, lower limb amyotrophy, severe kyphoscoliosis, and craniofacial abnormalities. The pathogenesis of LBWC remains unclear, with hypotheses including early amnion rupture, vascular disruptions, and embryonic developmental errors. Diagnosis is typically made by prenatal ultrasound in the first trimester. LBWC is generally lethal, warranting pregnancy termination. While multiple pregnancies may increase the risk, discordant presentation in monochorionic twins remains exceptionally rare.
