title: Contrasting Patterns of Cortical Volume Change in First-Episode Schizophrenia-Spectrum Psychosis
abstract: Importance Average gray matter volume (GMV) loss in early psychosis may conceal clinically relevant differences in brain change. Objective To identify longitudinal GMV-change patterns, their cross-site correspondence, and clinical associations. Design, Setting, and Participants Prospective cohort with T1-weighted MRI acquired during 2011–2026 at 2 Czech sites; median follow-up, approximately 13 months. Participants were 222 patients with first-episode schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis and 178 healthy controls frequency-matched by site and baseline age. Exposure First-episode psychosis vs healthy control status. Main Outcomes and Measures Diagnosis-blind clustering by site of image-quality-corrected, subsequently annualized GMV change across 333 cortical parcels; longitudinal voxel-based morphometry (VBM); Global Assessment of Functioning and consensus 5-factor Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale negative-symptom scores. Results Among 400 participants (mean [SD] age, 28.2 [7.5] years), 208 (52.0%) were male. Each site independently yielded 3 clusters: C1 (near-stable GMV), C2 (pronounced decrease), and C3 (increase). Cross-site centroid correlations across 333 parcels were strong for C2 and C3 (Spearman ρ = 0.865 and 0.861); C1 correlation was weak (ρ = 0.138), as expected for near-zero profiles with little regional variation. C2/C3 correspondence supported pooling matched site-specific clusters for post hoc analyses. Pooled clusters contained 77 patients and 125 controls in C1, 66 patients and 16 controls in C2, and 79 patients and 37 controls in C3. Suffixes −P and −HC identify patient and control subgroups. To situate patient changes relative to controls, post hoc VBM revealed an unanticipated gradient of increasingly pronounced GMV reduction across C1-HC → C1-P → C2-P, prominently involving association cortex, and bilateral ventral temporal GMV increase in C3-P (familywise error–corrected P < .05). The opposite contrast along this ordering showed periventricular changes consistent with progressively greater ventricular enlargement. C2-P had the lowest mean follow-up functioning and highest mean negative-symptom severity (adjusted omnibus P = .005 and .02); clinical changes from baseline did not differ significantly among patient groups. Conclusions and Relevance Early GMV change in psychosis was not uniform but comprised two contrasting directions: a clinically relevant, control-anchored pattern of increasingly pronounced GMV loss involving default mode regions and a distinct, directionally opposing ventral temporal increase. Key Points Question What patterns of cortical gray matter volume change emerge over approximately 1 year after first-episode schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis? Findings In this 2-site cohort of 222 patients and 178 controls, nearly two-thirds of patients lay along a gradient from near-stability in controls to widespread volume decrease, whereas one-third showed an opposing ventral temporal increase. Follow-up functioning and negative symptoms differed significantly among patient groups, with the least favorable scores in those showing the greatest decrease. Meaning Directions of within-person brain change may capture clinically relevant heterogeneity obscured by average volume loss.

title: Age-, sex-, and ethnicity-stratified CMR strain reference ranges and centile-based categories from the Healthy Hearts Consortium
abstract: Background This study presents reference ranges for cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived myocardial strain from the Healthy Hearts Consortium, while evaluating variations by demographic characteristics (age, sex, and ethnicity) and technical factors (scanner vendor, magnetic field strength). We derived reference ranges and centile-based categories for ventricular, atrial, and rapid strain parameters. The prognostic relevance of these categories was assessed by examining their associations with incident cardiovascular events. Methods The dataset included 9,088 CMR studies. Automated image analysis pipelines were established using suiteHEART (NeoSoft Inc.) and cvi42 (Circle Cardiovascular Imaging). A three-step quality control framework was applied including exclusion of incomplete data, visual assessment of image and segmentation quality, and statistical outlier removal. Ventricular strain and strain rate were measured using both software solutions. Additional cvi42-derived metrics included velocity and displacement, annular plane systolic excursion metrics, and rapid strain parameters. Age- and sex-specific reference ranges were generated using lambda–mu–sigma (LMS) modeling with penalized splines. Reference ranges were defined as values between the 2.5 th and 97.5 th percentiles. For lower-tail classification, values below the 2.5th percentile were considered mildly out-of-range and values below the 0.5th percentile at least moderately out-of-range. Differences across scanner vendors (Siemens, Philips, GE) and magnetic field strengths (1.5 T vs. 3 T) were evaluated using adjusted linear models. The prognostic relevance of selected cvi42-derived categories was evaluated in approximately 45,000 UK Biobank participants using Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and body mass index. Results After quality control, 8,975 CMR examinations (cvi42) and 8,992 (suiteHEART) were available for analysis; these represent software-specific analytic cohorts. Most exclusions occurred during visual quality control. Women had higher absolute ventricular and atrial strain values than men across all age groups. Left ventricular (LV) longitudinal strain and strain rate were slightly lower in older ages, whereas circumferential and radial parameters remained largely stable. Left atrial strain was also lower in older age groups, while right atrial strain did not vary by age. Annular plane systolic excursion and rapid strain metrics showed similar sex-specific patterns, with modestly lower atrial and displacement values in older groups. Ethnicity-related differences were modest, heterogeneous, and substantially smaller in magnitude than age- and sex-related differences. Technical effects were parameter specific. While LV longitudinal and circumferential strains were largely unaffected, radial strain was higher at 3 T and showed vendor-related differences. LMS-derived reference ranges and centile thresholds were applied both across all ethnicities and within ethnicity-specific analyses, and are presented stratified by age and sex. In the prognostic analysis, centile categories were most consistently associated with incident heart failure. LV longitudinal, circumferential, and radial strain below the 0.5th centile were associated with significantly increased risk of incident heart failure (HRs: 9.9 to 12.4, 95% CIs 7.00–13.90 to 8.49–18.06). Conclusion This study provides age- and sex-specific reference ranges and centile-based categories for CMR-derived strain parameters in a large reference population. Age and sex represent the primary determinants of myocardial deformation, whereas scanner-related effects are parameter-specific. Values in the lower extremes of the healthy reference distribution, particularly for LV strain, are associated with increased risk of incident heart failure. These findings enable standardized, centile-based classification of myocardial strain, facilitating consistent interpretation and improving risk stratification in research and clinical practice.

title: Integration of Neuroimaging and Histopathology in a Squirrel Monkey Model of Spontaneous Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy and Amyloid-Related Imaging Abnormalities
abstract: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) is a prevalent cerebrovascular pathology in AD and contributes to amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA), a major complication of current anti-amyloid immunotherapy. Despite its growing clinical importance, critical gaps remain in the development of reliable biomarkers for antemortem diagnosis of CAA. Squirrel monkeys (SQMs) are a valuable non-human primate model with translational relevance due to their universal propensity to develop abundant CAA and spontaneous ARIA in geriatric animals. The present study employed R 2 *, the apparent transverse relaxation rate, which is sensitive to susceptibility-related tissue properties, including iron content and blood oxygenation levels, to monitor age-related brain pathology in SQMs with varying CAA severity. Young, early geriatric, and late geriatric SQMs underwent 7T MRI using a dual-purpose T 2 *-w 3D multi-gradient-echo sequence for high-resolution anatomy and quantitative R 2 * mapping, alongside T 2 -w/FLAIR imaging. Whole-brain and gray matter R 2 * increased with age. In contrast, white matter R 2 * showed an initial increase followed by a late-life reversal, likely reflecting age-related changes in myelin integrity, tissue microstructure, and tissue water content. MRI-histopathology correlation linked T 2 *-w MRI hypointensities to CAA-positive iron-laden vessels associated with perivascular inflammation and, in some cases, hemosiderin deposits. Here we confirmed the occurrence of ARIA-H and ARIA-E events in geriatric animals. SQMs provided a valuable opportunity to examine the underlying pathology of spontaneous ARIA-E, revealing distinctive tissue signatures associated with its manifestation. ARIA-E hyperintensities were characterized by reactive gliosis and BBB disruption, whereas more advanced lesions exhibited perivascular lymphocytic infiltration and evidence of myelin and axonal injury. The current study presents compelling evidence linking R 2 * alterations with CAA severity and ARIA-related tissue injury, providing a foundation for further advancing early detection of CAA, ARIA risk assessment, and treatment strategies.

title: Normative transcriptomic clues to thalamic developmental vulnerability in C9orf7 2-FTLD
abstract: C9orf72 encodes a protein that is important for both typical neurodevelopment and homeostatic processes across the lifespan. Pathogenic C9orf72 repeat expansions constitute the most common genetic cause of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD). Collectively, preclinical models and clinical neuroimaging studies have observed smaller thalamic volumes in C9orf72 -associated FTLD, including in asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 repeat expansion carriers across 18 to 30 years old, supportive of potential neurodevelopmental origins. However, it is unknown whether asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers demonstrate volume differences in specific thalamic nuclei, as reported in older asymptomatic carriers and symptomatic patients; if so, normative transcriptomic patterns could reveal relevant neurodevelopmental and/or FTLD-related neurodegenerative processes. This study investigated volumetric MRI differences of the thalamic nuclei in asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers compared to non-carriers, and examined spatial associations with normative thalamic transcriptomics from 8 weeks post-conception through middle age. Young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers ( n =72) and non-carriers ( n =48) were enrolled in the Frontotemporal Dementia Prevention Initiative across Europe, Canada, and the USA (ages: 18-30 years; sex: 57% female). Spatial associations between young adult thalamic nuclei volumes and normative transcriptomics from the Allen Human Brain Atlas were examined using complementary data-driven and hypothesis-driven approaches. Spatial expression patterns of transcripts of interest were characterized across prenatal and postnatal neurodevelopment using BrainSpan data. Smaller volumes of the pulvinar, mediodorsal, and lateral nuclei were observed in young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers compared to non-carriers. These nuclei showed higher normative expression of transcripts involved concurrently in neurodevelopmental and C9orf72 -associated FTLD neurodegenerative processes (including lysosomal, autophagic, and small GTPase functions), and lower normative expression of CALB1 , a marker of prenatal human thalamic development. Normative expression of CALB2 (another human thalamic development marker) yielded positive correlations with C9orf72 across prenatal development to adulthood. These findings identify candidate transcripts that may provide insight into the molecular architecture leading to smaller thalamic nuclei volumes in C9orf72 -associated FTLD.

This study investigated volumetric MRI differences of the thalamic nuclei in asymptomatic young adult  C9orf72 expansion carriers compared to non-carriers, and examined spatial associations with normative thalamic transcriptomics from 8 weeks post-conception through middle age.  Young adult  C9orf72 expansion carriers (  n =72) and non-carriers (  n =48) were enrolled in the Frontotemporal Dementia Prevention Initiative across Europe, Canada, and the USA (ages: 18-30 years; sex: 57% female). Spatial associations between young adult thalamic nuclei volumes and normative transcriptomics from the Allen Human Brain Atlas were examined using complementary data-driven and hypothesis-driven approaches. Spatial expression patterns of transcripts of interest were characterized across prenatal and postnatal neurodevelopment using BrainSpan data. title: Population-based Ethnoracial Disparity in Life’s Essential 8 Vascular Health, Cerebral Small Vessel Disease & Cognition
abstract: Background Whether ethnoracial differences in cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) appear in multimarker burden, particular MRI manifestations, or both, and how they relate to Life’s Essential 8 (LE8) cardiovascular health and cognition, is unclear. Methods This cross-sectional study included 44,982 participants and an age- and sex-matched subsample of 1,426 with reviewed lacune and cerebral microbleed (CMB) ratings. White, South Asian, Black, Chinese and Mixed participants were compared on 0–2 (white matter hyperintensity [WMH]/enlarged perivascular space [ePVS]) and 0–4 (adding CMB and lacunes) composite scores and each marker. LE8 was related to WMH and composite burden, and cognitive means were compared by group. Models were age-, sex- and center-adjusted with false-discovery-rate correction. Results Both composite scores differed across groups (0–2: P=0.00010; 0–4: P=0.0011), with greater burden in Black than South Asian (0–4: OR 1.66; 95% CI, 1.21–2.28) and Chinese participants (OR 2.36; 1.51–3.70), whereas Black–White contrasts were not detected. Black participants had higher WMH volume than White participants (β=0.209; 0.110–0.308), robust to deprivation adjustment and segmentation method; South Asian participants had fewer ePVS (0.82; 0.72–0.93). No ethnoracial-group differences in lacune or CMB counts were detected after correction. Higher LE8 was associated with lower WMH volume (β=−0.13 per SD; −0.17 to −0.09) and lower two-marker burden (OR 0.89 per SD; 0.87–0.91) without detected ethnoracial moderation. Black participants, who had the least favorable LE8 scores, and South Asian participants had lower global cognition than White participants (z −0.76 and −0.57 versus 0.24) despite differing WMH profiles; the pooled WMH–cognition association was null. Conclusions Ethnoracial differences in multimarker cSVD burden were evident but marker-dependent: WMH showed the clearest Black–White difference; focal-lesion contrasts were inconclusive. Better cardiovascular health related to lower WMH and aggregate cSVD burden across groups, whereas cognitive differences did not track cSVD burden, supporting prospective prevention and cognition studies.

title: In Silico Metrological Assessment of 2D ROI Sampling Error Versus Whole-Organ 3D Volumetric CT Attenuation in Hepatic Steatosis: A Multicenter Monte Carlo Simulation on 971 Scans
abstract: PurposeTo quantify the metrological sampling error of conventional 2D regions of interest (ROIs) relative to whole-organ 3D volumetric CT attenuation ground truth in opportunistic screening for hepatic steatosis, and to evaluate its functional dependency on intraparenchymal spatial heterogeneity. Materials and MethodsIn this retrospective computational investigation adhering to CLAIM and TRIPOD-AI reporting standards, 971 non-contrast and contrast-enhanced abdominal CT examinations were analyzed across a multicenter derivation cohort (TotalSegmentator v2, n = 841) and an external validation cohort (Medical Segmentation Decathlon Task03 Liver, n = 130). Automated 3D liver segmentation was conducted using nnU-Net, supplemented by an 8-mm spherical 3D morphological erosion to eliminate peripheral partial volume effects, liver capsule artifacts, and major hilar vascular structures. Three clinical sampling paradigms (1, 3, and 5 axial circular 2D ROIs of 15 mm diameter) were simulated through 500 stochastic Monte Carlo iterations per examination (485,500 total simulations). Absolute metrological sampling error (|{Delta}HU| = |HU_ROI - HU_3D|) and diagnostic steatosis misclassification rates at the standard unenhanced threshold (HU_3D [≤] 40 HU) were evaluated. Statistical significance across sampling paradigms was tested using two-tailed paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. ResultsIn the derivation cohort (n = 841), the conventional guideline-recommended 3-ROI paradigm yielded a mean absolute sampling error of 6.61 {+/-} 7.83 HU (median: 2.92 HU; interquartile range: 1.34-8.45 HU). While representing a 41.6% error reduction compared to the single-ROI approach (11.32 {+/-} 14.16 HU; W = 0, p < 0.001), it demonstrated significant residual error compared to the extended 5-ROI approach (5.21 {+/-} 6.00 HU; W = 8, p < 0.001). Intraparenchymal spatial heterogeneity ({sigma}_HU) strongly predicted sampling error (Pearson r = 0.850, 95% CI: 0.830-0.868, p < 0.001). In borderline attenuation zones (35-45 HU), diagnostic misclassification reached 45.2% in heterogeneous livers. Findings were replicated in the external validation cohort (mean |{Delta}HU| = 7.38 HU for 1 ROI vs. 5.14 HU for 3 ROIs, p < 0.001). ConclusionManual 2D ROI sampling exhibits an inherent physical uncertainty that exceeds the 5-HU clinical tolerance threshold in parenchymally heterogeneous livers, misclassifying nearly half of borderline examinations. Accurate opportunistic steatosis screening requires transition to automated whole-organ 3D volumetric CT densitometry embedded in PACS networks. KEY POINTSO_LIConventional 3-ROI sampling leaves an average metrological error of 6.61 {+/-} 7.83 HU compared with 3D whole-liver ground truth. C_LIO_LIIntraparenchymal spatial heterogeneity is the primary determinant of 2D sampling error (r = 0.850, p < 0.001). C_LIO_LIIn borderline diagnostic attenuation ranges (35-45 HU), 2D manual sampling misclassifies up to 45.2% of patients with spatial heterogeneity. C_LI

title: Ex-vivo 7T MRI for accurate margin assessment in oral squamous cell carcinoma surgery
abstract: IntroductionResection margins in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) are frequently inadequate. This study investigated the accuracy and diagnostic performance of ex-vivo 7T MRI against histology. MethodsFifty OSCC specimens underwent ex-vivo 7T MRI. Tumours were segmented on corresponding histology and twice on MRI: blinded to histology (radiologist segmentation; clinical practice) and using histology (histology-MR segmentation; MR-based ground truth). Resection margins were measured in five regions and compared with histology. ResultsAnterior and posterior margins were generally smaller on MRI than on histology (maximum mean difference -2.5 mm), whereas cranial, caudal and deep margins were generally larger on MRI (mean differences <1 mm). For close margins (<5 mm), sensitivity was 95% for histology-MR segmentations and 91% for radiologist segmentations, with 75% specificity for both. ConclusionEx-vivo 7T MRI accurately measures resection margins and detects close margins with high sensitivity. A future clinical trial will determine whether intraoperative implementation reduces inadequate margins and adjuvant treatment.

title: MRI Biomarkers for Brain Metastases in Lung Cancer Using Machine Learning
abstract: Purpose Existing prognostic models for brain metastases from lung cancer rely on clinical variables and do not capture the biological heterogeneity of host or tumor factors underlying survival outcomes. We evaluated whether MRI-derived radiomic biomarkers improve prognostic stratification beyond clinical variables. We also investigated their biological correlates using matched histopathology. Experimental Design This retrospective study included 103 patients with brain metastases from lung cancer and matched pre-operative MRI and histopathology. Radiomic features from T1-weighted contrast-enhanced and T2-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery sequences were combined with clinical variables to train Cox proportional hazards, random survival forest, and DeepSurv models for overall survival (OS), CNS progression, and leptomeningeal (LM) progression. Risk groups from an imaging-only model were compared for clinical and histopathologic differences. Results Imaging features improved prognostic performance beyond clinical variables across all modeling frameworks, with the combined clinical-imaging DeepSurv model achieving the highest concordance index for OS (0.728). Risk groups from the best-performing model for each endpoint differed significantly in OS (median 26.7 vs. 9.1 months, p < 0.001) and LM progression ( p = 0.003), but not in CNS progression. Imaging-only risk groups did not differ significantly in any clinical variable, but high-risk patients were less likely to have tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (46% vs. 77%, p = 0.010) and PD-L1 expression ≥ 50% (10% vs. 32%, p = 0.049). Conclusions MRI radiomic biomarkers provide prognostic information beyond established clinical variables in lung cancer brain metastases and correspond to features of the tumor immune microenvironment, supporting their potential to refine risk stratification. Statement of Translational Relevance Brain metastases affect 30-40% of patients with lung cancer. Existing prognostic models rely on clinical variables, which do not fully capture the biological heterogeneity that drives outcomes. We show that machine learning models integrating MRI-derived radiomic features with clinical variables improve prognostic discrimination beyond clinical variables alone. Because these biomarkers are derived from standard-of-care pre-operative imaging, they can be generated without additional testing or delay to treatment planning. Using matched histopathology from resected lesions, we further show that imaging-defined risk groups do not simply reproduce established clinical risk factors but instead correspond to differences in the tumor immune microenvironment, including tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and PD-L1 expression. These findings support the use of quantitative imaging biomarkers as a non-invasive method to refine risk stratification at diagnosis, informing treatment selection and clinical trial enrollment for patients with brain metastases from lung cancer.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Modeling to Aid in the Identification of Genetic Conditions in Infants with Congenital Heart Disease
abstract: Background: Genetic conditions are common in congenital heart disease (CHD) and affect care, but are often missed or diagnosed late. We asked whether routine clinical data can shortlist the most likely genetic conditions. Methods: Retrospective single-center cohort of children with CHD and an echocardiogram who had either a confirmed genetic diagnosis or negative cytogenetic testing and CHD gene sequencing. Echocardiogram images and serial medical record data were added as model inputs in the order they become clinically available. Class balanced logistic regression (LR) and a multimodal deep learning fusion network were fitted to the same inputs at each step. The primary metric was balanced top-3 accuracy (correct diagnosis among the top three, averaged across conditions), with bootstrap intervals. Results: The cohort included 1,720 children (988 with common CHD-associated genetic conditions, 231 rare diagnoses, 501 negative testing). Using only inputs generated at the echocardiogram visit, LR reached a balanced top-3 accuracy 0.758 (chance 0.429). Serial records, radiology notes and ICD-10 codes, raised this to 0.809. Multimodal fusion performed similarly at each stage. With a genetic condition withheld from training, the fusion embedding placed affected children nearest to others sharing a gene group in 0.37 of cases versus 0.10 without the embedding (+0.268 [95% CI +0.242, +0.295]). Conclusions: Routine clinical data available at first echocardiogram can help identify likely genetic diagnoses, and later coded inputs ceiling. Multimodal fusion added no accuracy over LR, but places children sharing a genetic cause near one another, making nearest-neighbor retrieval informative for undiagnosed children.

title: Fever and Painful Skin Lesions: When to Consider Sweet's Syndrome.
abstract: Sweet's syndrome is an acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis characterised by fever, neutrophilia, and painful cutaneous lesions. We describe a case of a 31-year-old male admitted with a two-week history of fever up to 39°C and painful erythematous papules, scattered and coalescing into plaques over the trunk and limbs, together with pustules on an erythematous base over the palms and dorsum of the hands. No relevant epidemiological exposure or recent drug exposure was identified. Investigation showed an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 40 mm/h, leucocytosis of 14,380/µL with 77% neutrophils and no eosinophilia, and a C-reactive protein of 1.21 mg/dL. Liver and renal function, albumin, lactate dehydrogenase, serum iron, ferritin, and serum protein electrophoresis were normal, and a respiratory viral panel was negative. Blood, urine, and pustule cultures, an interferon-gamma release assay, and serology for human immunodeficiency virus, syphilis, hepatitis A, B, C, and E viruses, cytomegalovirus, and Epstein-Barr virus were negative, as was an autoantibody panel. Serum immunoglobulin A was below the detection limit (<0.07 g/L) before corticosteroid therapy and on all repeat measurements, including after treatment had been discontinued, with normal immunoglobulin G and M, and IgG-based coeliac serology was negative. Computed tomography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis and peripheral blood immunophenotyping showed no abnormalities. A skin biopsy demonstrated intraepidermal blisters and a superficial perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate without vasculitis, spongiform pustules, or psoriasiform changes. The clinical and laboratory criteria for classical Sweet's syndrome were fulfilled, and the histology was compatible with, although not classical for, the syndrome. Prednisolone 60 mg/day (approximately 0.6 mg/kg/day) was started on clinical suspicion of the syndrome. After one week, the fever had resolved, but the lesions worsened slightly, prompting escalation to 100 mg/day (approximately 1 mg/kg/day), after which they regressed progressively and resolved completely within three weeks of dose escalation, with normalisation of the leucocyte count. Corticosteroids were tapered and discontinued before the three-month assessment, at which there was no relapse and no evidence of malignancy. This case illustrates three practical points: an acral pustular morphology does not exclude the diagnosis; early worsening under corticosteroid therapy may reflect an initial dose insufficient for body weight rather than an incorrect diagnosis, once infection has been rigorously excluded; and the coexisting finding of selective immunoglobulin A deficiency carries independent implications for coeliac disease screening and long-term follow-up.

title: Managing Severe Proximal Femoral Fibrous Dysplasia in a Young Adult Using Hemiarthroplasty in a Resource-Constrained Healthcare System: A Case Report.
abstract: Fibrous dysplasia of the proximal femur may lead to progressive deformity, pain, and pathological fractures, with shepherd's crook deformity representing one of its most severe manifestations. Although valgus osteotomy with intramedullary fixation is considered the preferred surgical treatment, extensive bone destruction and limited healthcare resources may preclude conventional reconstruction. We present a case of severe proximal femoral fibrous dysplasia successfully managed with bipolar cemented hemiarthroplasty in a resource-constrained healthcare setting. A 25-year-old man presented with progressive left hip pain, severe proximal femoral deformity, and impaired ambulation. Radiographic evaluation demonstrated lateral bowing of the proximal femur, while histopathological examination following core biopsy confirmed fibrous dysplasia. Internal fixation using an intramedullary nail was initially planned; however, intraoperative findings revealed extensive fibro-osseous replacement, severely compromised bone quality, and inadequate cortical support, making stable fixation technically impossible. Because more complex reconstructive procedures were not covered by the national health insurance system, a bipolar cemented hemiarthroplasty, augmented with plate fixation of the osteotomized fragments, was performed as a salvage procedure. The postoperative course was uneventful, with marked pain relief, improved gait, and satisfactory functional recovery at 10 months of follow-up (Oxford Hip Score 34/48). Conventional fixation for shepherd's crook deformity requires adequate residual cortical bone to achieve stable implant fixation. In cases with extensive cortical destruction and bone stock too thin to support reliable press-fit fixation, cemented hemiarthroplasty may represent a practical alternative. Preservation of the native acetabulum may also reduce postoperative instability while providing satisfactory functional outcomes. title: Regime-Aware Router Learning for Multi-Domain Medical Image Generation with Diffusion Experts
abstract: Heterogeneous medical image data motivate domain-specialized diffusion experts, but expert specialization alone does not determine how their predictions should be combined during sampling. Learning a global router is particularly challenging when the server has limited, potentially unrepresentative images. We study two router-learning strategies for a fixed expert pool. Server-Only learns input- and timestep-dependent expert assignments from server images with component labels. Anchor-Delta (AD) uses the same images and frozen experts to obtain additional evidence from denoising losses. It distills targets that combine this evidence with the current router's assignments, while a proxy gate controls a subsequent refinement step. Component labels describe data origin; expert losses measure empirical prediction performance. We evaluate these distinct signals through routing analyses and paired medical image generation. An AD-trained router improves generation metrics over Server-Only in a heterogeneous four-domain setting, and a separate server-data study shows gains in held-out routing over a corrected-routing comparator. Additional paired evaluations show that the effect of inference-time evidence mixing varies across benchmarks. These findings establish server-data availability and expert performance as distinct considerations in learning routers for multi-domain diffusion models.

title: A Concept-informed Interpretable Artificial Intelligence Framework for Breast Ultrasound Diagnosis
abstract: Most existing artificial intelligence systems for breast ultrasound rely primarily on image-driven prediction, with limited incorporation of the knowledge from the Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS) and the intermediate assessment processes underlying radiologists' workflow, thereby constraining their interpretability and alignment with clinical practice. We curated, to our knowledge, the largest multicenter collection of breast ultrasound images paired with structured BI-RADS descriptors, comprising 9,941 patients across 20 independent datasets. Across 14 testing datasets, IBUS demonstrated consistent generalization performance across different clinical centers and imaging conditions. Incorporating BI-RADS descriptors enabled fine-grained risk stratification, while cross-checking predicted BI-RADS grades against malignancy probabilities identified internally discordant predictions that may warrant additional clinical review. In a reader study involving eight radiologists, IBUS assistance increased diagnostic sensitivity among both junior and senior readers, with the potential of guiding radiologists to make targeted revision in risk stratification. Overall, IBUS exhibits its potential as a second-stage decision-support system that complements radiologists by providing additional risk estimates and interpretable evidence for diagnostically challenging cases. The demo video of IBUS platform is publicly available at https://github.com/zsz1997/IBUS.

title: Explicitly Aligned Multi-View Breast Cancer Risk Prediction from Variable-Length Screening Histories
abstract: Accurate breast cancer risk prediction from screening mammography is essential for improved risk stratification and personalized screening. It can benefit from both temporal breast tissue changes across longitudinal examinations and complementary anatomical information from craniocaudal (CC) and mediolateral oblique (MLO) views. Leveraging longitudinal information requires identifying corresponding tissue regions across examinations, yet most approaches rely on implicit feature alignment without explicitly enforcing spatial consistency. Recent work has demonstrated the benefits of explicit temporal alignment; however, existing methods model each view independently, preventing them from exploiting complementary CC and MLO information. Furthermore, explicit approaches have been limited to a single prior examination. To fill these gaps, we propose (github.com/sot176/FlexLMV-Net), a breast-wise longitudinal multi-view framework that jointly models CC and MLO views across screening examinations while accommodating a variable number of prior examinations. FlexLMV-Net explicitly aligns longitudinal feature maps and integrates complementary views through cross-view temporal fusion and a dual-stream attention block. Evaluated on EMBED and CSAW-CC, FlexLMV-Net consistently outperforms existing approaches across breast density, cancer subtypes, and demographic subgroups, highlighting the benefits of explicit longitudinal alignment, multi-view modeling, and flexible use of available screening history. We further introduce (github.com/sot176/BCRBench), an open-source benchmark that unifies state-of-the-art single- and multi-timepoint breast cancer risk prediction models under standardized preprocessing, training, inference, and evaluation protocols, enabling fair and reproducible comparison of existing methods.

title: NoduleFlow: Automatic 3D Lung Nodule Detection and Segmentation
abstract: Low dose Computed Tomography (CT) is the standard imaging modality for lung cancer screening. On CT scans, lung cancer typically manifests as pulmonary nodules, whose manual identification is time-consuming and prone to observer variability, image quality limitations, and suboptimal reading conditions. Moreover, subtle temporal changes are often difficult to quantify reliably in CT scans from the same patient across follow-up examinations. Deep learning-based approaches for the automatic detection and segmentation of lung nodules have demonstrated improved accuracy and efficiency. However, most existing approaches provide only coarse region-of-interest localisation, rely on prior lesion annotations or human supervision, or treat detection and segmentation as separate tasks. In this work, we present NoduleFlow, a framework for lung nodule detection, classification, and segmentation directly from series of CT volumes. Our proposal consists of four interconnected modules and operates in an automated manner at inference time, without requiring prior lesion annotations, manual initialisation, or region-of-interest pre-selection. We further investigate whether nodule localization benefits from the propagation of candidate regions across follow-up scans through inter-scan registration fields, as opposed to conventional independent per-scan analysis. The generalisability of the framework is systematically evaluated across four independent datasets. The results underscore the potential of automated pipelines for lung nodule analysis in screening and diagnostic settings.

title: Neuromorphic Decoding and Dynamical Image Reconstruction from Populations of Spiking Retinal Ganglion Cells
abstract: Decoding visual stimuli from the spiking activity of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) informs both our understanding of the retinal code and the design of visual prostheses. Natural vision is dynamic, yet state-of-the-art decoders mostly reconstruct single frames with artificial neural networks that process dense, continuous-valued signals rather than the retina's sparse, asynchronous spikes. We asked whether dynamic scenes can be reconstructed and tracked entirely within the spike domain, and at what computational cost. We built an end-to-end spiking neural network (SNN) whose neurons integrate the recorded RGC spikes over time. Populations of up to 1836 RGCs were recorded ex vivo from mouse retina on high-density microelectrode arrays while flashed images, moving bars, drifting gratings and randomly moving handwritten digits were presented. For moving digits, one shared spiking encoder fed two readouts, one reconstructing the image and one decoding the digit's position. Compute energy was estimated from counted synaptic operations. The SNN decoded what and where at once. It reconstructed the stimuli with a structural similarity (SSIM) of up to 0.93, refining the reconstruction as spikes accumulated, and tracked a randomly moving target with a mean error of 1.33 pixels on a $32\times32$ grid. Its fidelity nearly matched that of the best of 17 larger spiking and artificial decoders (5.9 million to 1.7 billion parameters, versus 5.4 million), and at a mean firing rate of 14.2% it needed an estimated $\sim$70-fold less compute energy than a dense artificial network of the same architecture. Dynamic visual scenes can thus be decoded from retinal population activity in the spike domain, with a compact network and at a compute cost compatible with implantable and wearable neural interfaces, supporting spike-native decoders for visual prostheses.

title: MID: Mask-Image Distributional Divergence for Evaluating Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Current evaluation protocols for medical image segmentation remain largely anchored in sample-wise comparisons, e.g., Dice and Hausdorff distance, which require each prediction to be paired with a ground-truth mask. Yet two limitations arise in practice: they are inapplicable when predictions are made on unlabeled data; and even when annotations are available, they cannot assess whether a collection of predictions matches the distributional structure of the ground-truth population. We introduce MID (Mask-Image Distributional Divergence), a distribution-level evaluation metric for medical image segmentation. MID builds upon the observation that segmentation quality is a property of the joint image-mask distribution: a mask may be anatomically plausible in isolation yet incorrect for the image it accompanies. MID compares the joint distribution of images and masks between a reference set and a set of predictions, without requiring sample-wise correspondence. This captures both mask realism and image-mask consistency. We evaluate MID across 13 publicly available datasets spanning CT, MRI, and MRA. Under anatomically realistic corruptions across 56 organ groups, MID tracks mean Dice and Hausdorff distance without per-sample ground-truth pairing. MID also detects distributional shifts across modalities and anatomies, identifies image-mask misalignment through controlled shuffling experiments, and produces reliable model rankings across real segmentation models. Official implementation available at github.com/erc-caravel/pytorch-mid

title: Higher Preoperative Magnetic Resonance Imaging Use in Asia-Pacific Compared With North America for Pediatric Tibial Eminence Fractures: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate differences in the incidence, diagnosis, and management of pediatric tibial eminence fractures between the Asia-Pacific region and North America. Methods A systematic review and subjective synthesis was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. PubMed, MEDLINE, and Cochrane databases were searched from inception to May 1, 2025, using the keywords "tibial eminence" or "tibial spine" or "anterior cruciate ligament" and "fracture or avulsion." All original human surgical studies on pediatric tibial eminence fractures published in the Asia-Pacific region and North America were included, and data on the incidence, diagnosis, and treatment of pediatric tibial eminence fractures were collected. Results A total of 24 studies (9 from Asia-Pacific and 15 from North America) were selected with a total of 1973 patients. Subset analysis (of 6 Asia-Pacific and 3 North American studies) showed a trend toward higher rates of preoperative magnetic resonance imaging use among Asia-Pacific (96.3%-100%) compared with North American patients (36.2%-46.0%). There were also trends toward higher rates of arthroscopic reduction (compared with open reduction) and suture-based fixation (compared with screw fixation and other modalities) observed in Asia-Pacific patients compared with North American patients. Conclusions Asia-Pacific surgeons reported substantially higher preoperative magnetic resonance imaging use compared with North American surgeons, alongside potential trends toward greater use of arthroscopic reduction and suture-based fixation. Level of evidence Level IV, systematic review of Level III and IV studies.

title: Clinical and Sonographic Features of Neonatal Ovarian Cysts With Autoamputation.
abstract: Purpose Autoamputation is a rare but severe complication of neonatal ovarian cysts. This case series describes the clinical, sonographic, and pathological characteristics of neonatal ovarian cysts that progressed to autoamputation, compared with those that did not, based on a retrospective review of 19 cysts. We aim to help clinicians suspect autoamputation when managing complex neonatal ovarian cysts. Methods Medical records of 18 neonates (19 ovarian cysts) treated at two medical centers between January 2012 and December 2023 were reviewed. All cysts appeared complex on postnatal ultrasonography. We documented prenatal and postnatal sonographic features (cyst size, solid components, septations, fluid-debris levels, calcification), timing of examinations, intraoperative findings (adhesions, autoamputation), and pathology results. Descriptive statistics and exploratory comparisons between autoamputation (n = 9 cysts) and non-autoamputation (n = 10 cysts) groups were performed, without claims of predictive modeling. Results Of the 19 complex ovarian cysts, 9 (47.3%) were confirmed autoamputated at surgery. The autoamputation group showed a longer median interval from first complex features to surgery (68 vs. 21.5 days) and an older age at last postnatal ultrasound (11 vs. 1 days). Intra-abdominal adhesions were observed in 66.7% of autoamputation cases versus 10% of non-autoamputation cases. Follicles were absent in all autoamputated cysts on pathology but present in 90% of non-autoamputated cysts. Sonographic findings evolved over time: fluid-debris levels became the predominant feature with increasing duration, while calcification appeared late (22.2% in the autoamputation group). Conclusion Autoamputation of neonatal ovarian cysts was associated with a longer interval from first complex features to surgery, absence of follicles on pathology, and frequent intra-abdominal adhesions. Sonographic features evolved over time, with fluid-debris levels becoming common and calcification appearing late but with poor sonographic sensitivity. These observations may help clinicians better understand the evolution of complex neonatal ovarian cysts associated with autoamputation; however, the diagnostic and predictive value of these findings requires further validation.

title: Preoperative Functional Imaging Predicts Deep Brain Stimulation Outcome in Craniocervical Dystonia.
abstract: Background Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is an established treatment for craniocervical dystonia (CCD), yet postoperative benefit varies widely and cannot be estimated before surgery. Resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) has shown prognostic value across DBS indications. The objective of this study was to develop and externally validate preoperative rs-fMRI models estimating DBS response in CCD. Methods Forty-two patients from two independent centers underwent preoperative 3 T rs-fMRI (discovery, n = 26; validation, n = 16). Using 12 literature-informed, symptom-relevant regions of interest, we quantified the amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation as a measure of intrinsic regional neural activity. We applied regularized modeling to classify super-responders, distinguish responders from non-responders, and estimate improvement in Burke-Fahn-Marsden Dystonia Rating Scale motor subscore. Results When applied to the validation cohort, the imaging models achieved a three-category classification accuracy of 75.0% (50.5%-89.8%) using a sequential two-step procedure (P perm = 0.002). Predicted continuous improvement was also correlated with empirical improvement (R ext = 0.65, Q 2 = 0.34, P perm = 0.004). Within the discovery cohort, nested leave-one-out-cross-validation, in which feature selection and decision-threshold derivation were repeated independently within each training fold, yielded areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.73 (0.50-0.96) and 0.77 (0.51-1.00). Across models, baseline primary motor cortex activity was consistently associated with diminished postoperative benefit. Conclusions Preoperative rs-fMRI captures clinically relevant variation in baseline brain state in CCD, with predictive performance supported in an external validation. These findings provide preliminary support for rs-fMRI as a potential source of information to aid patient counseling and clinical decision-making, pending prospective validation. © 2026 International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.

Forty-two patients from two independent centers underwent preoperative 3 T rs-fMRI (discovery, n = 26; validation, n = 16). Using 12 literature-informed, symptom-relevant regions of interest, we quantified the amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation as a measure of intrinsic regional neural activity. We applied regularized modeling to classify super-responders, distinguish responders from non-responders, and estimate improvement in Burke-Fahn-Marsden Dystonia Rating Scale motor subscore.

Results

When applied to the validation cohort, the imaging models achieved a three-category classification accuracy of 75.0% (50.5%-89.8%) using a sequential two-step procedure (Pperm = 0.002). Predicted continuous improvement was also correlated with empirical improvement (Rext = 0.65, Q2 = 0.34, Pperm = 0.004). Within the discovery cohort, nested leave-one-out-cross-validation, in which feature selection and decision-threshold derivation were repeated independently within each training fold, yielded areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.73 (0.50-0.96) and 0.77 (0.51-1.00). Across models, baseline primary motor cortex activity was consistently associated with diminished postoperative benefit.

Conclusions

Preoperative rs-fMRI captures clinically relevant variation in baseline brain state in CCD, with predictive performance supported in an external validation. These findings provide preliminary support for rs-fMRI as a potential source of information to aid patient counseling and clinical decision-making, pending prospective validation. © 2026 International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.

title: Growth trajectory and miscarriage diagnosis threshold in early IVF pregnancy: multicenter study.
abstract: Objectives To characterize early-pregnancy ultrasound findings in pregnancies conceived via in-vitro fertilization (IVF) for which gestational age is known precisely based on the date of embryo transfer (ET), and to examine their association with first-trimester pregnancy outcome. Methods This was a retrospective multicenter cohort study of fresh- and frozen-cycle IVF pregnancies from 14 centers across England between January 2022 and December 2024, with one center contributing additional data from January 2019 to December 2021. Patients with a confirmed intrauterine pregnancy at the first transvaginal ultrasound scan (≤ 9 + 6 weeks' gestation) after ET were included for analysis of pregnancy outcome. Data collected included the date of ET, embryo stage at transfer, early-pregnancy ultrasound measurements, including crown-rump length (CRL) and mean sac diameter (MSD), and expected gestational age. The endpoint was viability at the 11-14-week dating scan. CRL growth was modeled against gestational age using quadratic regression. The diagnostic performance of a range of gestational-age cut-offs for identifying miscarriage was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity and positive predictive value (PPV). Results A total of 10 009 IVF pregnancies were included, of which 8223 (82.2%) were viable at 11-14 weeks and 1786 (17.8%) were non-viable. A significant difference was found in the distribution of CRL measurements at the first ultrasound scan between pregnancies that were found to be viable and those that were non-viable at the subsequent 11-14-week scan (P < 0.001). When stratified by gestational age based on the date of ET, viable pregnancies had a higher median CRL than pregnancies of the same gestational age that subsequently ended in miscarriage, although there was a degree of overlap in the distribution of CRL values between the two groups. Furthermore, among pregnancies that were viable at 11-14 weeks, significant variability was seen in CRL and MSD measurements at each gestational age. The estimated mean CRL growth rate was 0.926 mm/day from when CRL was first measurable. The ultrasound finding of an empty gestational sac at or beyond 47 days' gestation based on the date of ET (n = 406) had a PPV of 100% and specificity of 100% (95% CI, 94.9-100%) for first-trimester miscarriage. Conclusions Early-pregnancy ultrasound measurements in IVF pregnancy show wide physiological variability at any given gestational age, even when gestational age can be calculated precisely from the date of ET. An empty gestational sac at or beyond 47 days' gestation was associated with 100% PPV and 100% specificity for non-viable pregnancy. Further external validation in independent cohorts is required to confirm this potential threshold for diagnosing miscarriage in IVF pregnancy. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Comparative toxicity and efficacy of consolidative thoracic radiotherapy after first-line chemoimmunotherapy in extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer: real-world retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background First-line chemoimmunotherapy (CT-IT) is the standard treatment for extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC), while consolidative thoracic radiotherapy (cTRT) may improve local control and survival. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of cTRT after first-line CT-IT in patients with ES-SCLC in a real-world setting. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 199 patients with ES-SCLC who received first-line CT-IT. Patients were divided into a CT-IT + cTRT group (n = 97) and a CT-IT alone group (n = 102). Survival outcomes included progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). Treatment-related adverse events were assessed. Results The two groups were generally comparable at baseline, although the CT-IT + cTRT group had fewer brain metastases and more favorable response-related features after induction treatment. Median PFS and OS were significantly longer in the CT-IT + cTRT group (both P < 0.001). cTRT (P < 0.001) and a longer duration of maintenance immunotherapy (P = 0.031) were independently associated with a better PFS. For OS, cTRT was associated with better survival status (P = 0.003) and liver metastasis with poorer survival status (P = 0.015). Regarding safety, grade 1-2 dermatitis and gastrointestinal toxicity were more frequent in the CT-IT + cTRT group, whereas rates of pneumonitis, esophagitis, immune-related adverse events, and grade 3-4 toxicities were comparable between groups. Conclusion In this real-world retrospective cohort, the addition of cTRT to first-line CT-IT was associated with significantly improved PFS and OS in patients with ES-SCLC, without an apparent increase in severe treatment-related toxicity. Prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings and refine patient selection for cTRT.

title: Primary leiomyosarcoma arising adjacent to a femoral stem following total hip arthroplasty: a case report with radiologic and histopathological correlation.
abstract: Periprosthetic sarcomas associated with total hip arthroplasty (THA) are exceedingly rare, and most reported cases represent undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma or osteosarcoma. Primary leiomyosarcoma of bone is also an uncommon malignancy, accounting for less than 1% of primary malignant bone tumors. The occurrence of primary leiomyosarcoma adjacent to an orthopedic implant is therefore exceptionally rare. A 69-year-old woman presented with progressive left thigh pain 13 years after THA. Radiographs demonstrated osteolysis and cortical thinning at the distal femoral stem. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed an intramedullary lesion with cortical thinning and contrast enhancement. 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography-CT showed increased uptake at the lesion (SUV max, 11.9), without evidence of other primary tumors. The differential diagnoses included implant-related osteolysis, infection, metastatic tumor, and primary bone tumor. An open biopsy was performed, and a diagnosis of pleomorphic sarcoma was made. Wide resection with proximal femoral replacement was performed. Histopathological examination established the diagnosis of primary leiomyosarcoma of bone. Prominent lymphocytic infiltration and immunohistochemical findings, including p53 overexpression and partial loss of Rb expression, within the tumor, raise the possibility of chronic inflammation and associated molecular alterations as theoretical contributing factors to tumorigenesis. Periprosthetic sarcomas can mimic more common postoperative complications, making diagnosis challenging. Delayed diagnosis may adversely affect prognosis. This case highlights the importance of considering malignancy in atypical periprosthetic lesions and underscores the role of multimodality imaging and biopsy in achieving an accurate diagnosis.

title: Associations between tissue stiffness, tumor response to transarterial chemoembolization and prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma: insights from multifrequency 3D-magnetic resonance elastography.
abstract: Objectives To investigate the correlation between tissue stiffness, as measured across various target tissues using multifrequency three-dimensional magnetic resonance elastography (3D-MRE), and tumor responses to transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), as well as post-treatment prognosis in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods HCC patients scheduled for TACE treatment were prospectively recruited and received multifrequency 3D-MRE before the initiation of TACE procedure. Measurements of tumor stiffness (TS), liver stiffness (LS), and spleen stiffness (SS) were conducted at frequencies of 60 Hz and 30 Hz, respectively. Treatment response was assessed using the mRECIST. Patient follow-up was conducted to evaluate overall survival outcomes. Results The final patient cohort consisted of 43 patients (mean age: 56.66±10.13 years; 34 males), including 16 non-responders and 27 responders. Non-responders exhibited significantly elevated TS (4.10±2.54 vs. 2.68±1.61kPa, p=0.035), LS (2.88±1.43 vs. 1.97±0.59kPa, p=0.026), and SS (4.03±0.90 vs. 3.13±1.08kPa, p=0.008) at the frequency of 30Hz. Firth's penalized univariable logistic analysis identified age (adjusted odds ratio [OR]=0.93, P=0.036), tumor number (OR=0.69, P=0.035), LS at 60Hz (OR=0.79, p=0.046), TS at 30Hz (OR=0.73, p=0.037), LS at 30Hz (OR=0.44, p=0.008), and SS at 30Hz (OR=0.44, P=0.009) as potential predictors of treatment response. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for predicting treatment response was 0.69 for age, tumor number and TS at 30Hz, 0.67 for LS at both 60Hz and 30Hz, and 0.75 for SS at 30Hz. Univariable Cox regression identified TS at both 60Hz (hazard ratio=1.15, p=0.014) and 30Hz (hazard ratio=1.40, p=0.010) as potential predictors of overall survival. Conclusion Spleen stiffness measured at 30 Hz via 3D-MRE may serve as a potential predictor of treatment response to TACE in HCC patients, whereas tumor stiffness measured at both 60Hz and 30Hz appears to correlate with overall survival. Further research is necessary to validate these preliminary associations.

Spleen stiffness measured at 30 Hz via 3D-MRE may serve as a potential predictor of treatment response to TACE in HCC patients, whereas tumor stiffness measured at both 60Hz and 30Hz appears to correlate with overall survival. Further research is necessary to validate these preliminary associations.

title: A CAD-Based Workflow for Structured Mid-Sagittal Plane Definition in Contralateral Mandibular Mirroring: A Technical Note.
abstract: Objectives To describe a structured CAD-based workflow for defining the mandibular mid-sagittal plane during contralateral mirroring for unilateral mandibular defects and to demonstrate its clinical applicability in reconstructive planning. Methods DICOM data were segmented to generate a mandibular STL model. In CAD software, a mid-sagittal splitting plane was constructed using convergent geometric references, including a best-fit plane, principal inertia axis, and centre-of-gravity point, combined with pogonion as the anterior midline reference. The unaffected hemimandible was mirrored across this plane, exported as an STL file, and used for biomodel fabrication, guide planning, and reconstruction plate pre-contouring. A representative ameloblastoma case was used to illustrate the workflow. Results The workflow produced a mirrored mandibular template suitable for digital-to-physical transfer. In the representative case, the template supported preoperative reconstruction plate adaptation and intraoperative contour planning. At 12-month follow-up, facial contour and occlusion were clinically acceptable on qualitative assessment. Conclusions A convergent reference CAD workflow offers a practical method for standardising mid-sagittal plane definition in mandibular contralateral mirroring. The workflow may reduce reliance on subjective landmark selection in unilateral pathology; however, quantitative validation against established midplane methods is required. Clinical significance This technique provides a stepwise digital planning workflow for unilateral mandibular reconstruction, helping surgeons define the mid-sagittal plane, create mirrored templates, fabricate biomodels, and pre-contour reconstruction plates when tumour-related distortion limits reliable anatomical reference points. Level of evidence v This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. title: A short large-calibre intrapelvic arterial bridge between the superior and inferior gluteal arteries: an in vivo CT angiographic observation.
abstract: Purpose To describe a short, large-calibre intrapelvic arterial bridge between independently established superior and inferior gluteal arteries (SGA and IGA) and to distinguish it from a common gluteal trunk. Methods A pelvic computed tomography angiography (CTA) examination from a 40-year-old man was retrospectively analysed from an anonymised archive using multiplanar reformations, maximum-intensity projections, and three-dimensional vascular reconstructions. Linear and calibre measurements were obtained with workstation callipers and verified by independent review. Results On the right, the internal iliac artery divided after 34 mm into anterior and posterior trunks. The anterior trunk gave the obturator and internal pudendal arteries and continued as the IGA (2.6 mm); the posterior trunk gave sacral arteries and continued as the SGA (4.0 mm). The SGA and IGA were connected 44.2 mm distal to the internal iliac bifurcation by a 1.8-mm-long, 3.5-mm-calibre intrapelvic bridge. The SGA exited suprapiriformly and the IGA infrapiriformly. No corresponding bridge was present on the left. Conclusion The configuration differs from an Adachi Type II common SGA-IGA trunk because the two gluteal arteries are already anatomically separate before the communicating segment. Strict assignment to an Adachi type is not possible from this CTA alone because the umbilical continuation of the hypogastric axis is not demonstrated. Previous cadaveric studies documented SGA-IGA communications, whereas the present observation provides individual in vivo CTA topography and morphometry of a very short, large-calibre bridge.

title: [The eye as a mirror of the heart-retinal findings in heart failure and cardiovascular diseases].
abstract: Background Due to its unique anatomical and functional characteristics, the retina represents a promising organ for the evaluation of systemic vascular diseases. Modern imaging techniques, particularly optical coherence tomography angiography (OCT-A), enable noninvasive and quantitative assessment of retinal microcirculation. The aim of this review is to present current findings on the significance of retinal biomarkers in cardiovascular diseases, with a focus on heart failure. Results Numerous studies show associations between retinal vascular changes and arterial hypertension, coronary heart disease, left ventricular hypertrophy, and heart failure. Changes in retinal vascular parameters such as vascular density and perfusion density correlate with structural and functional cardiac changes. Patients with retinal vascular occlusions have an increased risk of stroke, myocardial infarction, and higher cardiovascular mortality. Initial studies in patients with acute decompensated heart failure have demonstrated changes in retinal vascular and perfusion density that can be reversed by recompensation. These observations led to the introduction of the term "cardio-ocular syndrome," which describes the interactions between cardiac function, systemic congestion, and retinal microcirculation. Conclusion Retinal imaging opens up new possibilities for the noninvasive assessment of systemic microcirculatory disorders in cardiovascular diseases. OCT‑A could contribute in the future to risk stratification, assessment of disease progression, and monitoring of therapy in heart failure.

title: The boundary between microbial detection and implant-related infection: a structured narrative review of analytical credibility, biological persistence, host response, and clinical causality.
abstract: Background Unexpected microbial signals are frequently encountered in patients with orthopaedic implants who do not satisfy validated criteria for confirmed infection. The central interpretive problem is not limited to periprosthetic joint infection (PJI); it also arises in fracture-fixation and spinal instrumentation, and it involves conventional culture, sonication, histopathology, broad-range polymerase chain reaction (PCR), 16 S rRNA sequencing, and metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS). Methods We performed a structured narrative review of literature identified in PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science, updated through 27 June 2026. Eligible publications addressed microbial or biofilm-associated signals in orthopaedic implants without unequivocal infection at the time of sampling, or reported outcomes after unexpected positive cultures. Evidence was organized by implant type, indication for implant removal, detection method, host-response evidence, and longitudinal outcome. Particular attention was paid to the distinction between routinely removed fracture-fixation devices and failure-related arthroplasty or spinal revisions. Results Routine removal of fracture-fixation devices provides the least confounded clinical window and demonstrates that microbial signals may be recovered from implants in the absence of recognized failure or overt infection. By contrast, arthroplasty and spinal cohorts labelled "presumed aseptic" are intrinsically confounded because pain, loosening, osteolysis, or pseudarthrosis may represent occult infection. Molecular positivity is further limited by low-biomass contamination and inability to distinguish viable organisms from relic DNA. Favorable outcomes after revision do not prove that infection was never present, because revision surgery itself may eradicate or substantially reduce an occult microbial burden. Conclusions Microbial detection should be interpreted through three sequential domains: analytical credibility, biological activity or persistence, and clinical causality supported by host response or implant-related pathology. "Stable coexistence" is best treated as a longitudinal clinical phenotype or testable mechanistic hypothesis, not as an established diagnostic category. This framework complements, but does not replace, validated PJI, fracture-related infection (FRI), or other implant-specific definitions.

title: Impact of puncture site location in percutaneous transhepatic gallbladder drainage on outcomes of subsequent laparoscopic cholecystectomy: a multicenter retrospective clinical study.
abstract: Background Percutaneous transhepatic gallbladder drainage (PTGD) followed by laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC) is an effective treatment strategy for acute cholecystitis (AC). However, the impact of the PTGD puncture site on subsequent LC outcomes has not been systematically investigated. Methods This retrospective study included patients diagnosed with AC who underwent PTGD followed by LC at the First Affiliated Hospital of Dalian Medical University (January 2018-May 2025) and Yingkou Central Hospital (January 2020-May 2025). PTGD was performed according to the Tokyo Guidelines 2018 (TG18) and individualized clinical judgment. Based on CT imaging, patients were categorized into two groups according to the PTGD puncture site: the fundus group (n = 208), where the puncture was adjacent to the gallbladder fundus, and the neck group (n = 47), where the puncture was adjacent to the gallbladder neck. Clinical parameters compared included baseline characteristics, gallbladder neck stone impaction, post-PTGD hospital stay, LC operative time, difficult gallbladder, intraoperative injuries and hemorrhage, post-LC complications, drainage placement and duration after LC, total hospital stay for LC, post-LC hospital stay, and hospitalization expenses. Multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses were performed to evaluate the independent association between puncture site and perioperative outcomes. Results In univariate analyses, no significant differences were observed between the fundus and neck groups regarding intraoperative injuries or major postoperative complications. Compared with the neck group, the fundus group demonstrated significantly shorter LC operative time, a lower incidence of difficult gallbladder, fewer drainage placements and shorter drainage duration after LC, reduced post-LC hospital stay, and lower hospitalization expenses (P < 0.05). In multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses, after adjusting for sex, age, body mass index (BMI), gallbladder neck stone impaction, interval between PTGD and LC, and TG18 severity grade, fundus-adjacent puncture remained independently associated with a lower risk of difficult gallbladder, reduced drainage placements and shorter drainage duration after LC, shorter post-LC and total hospital stays, and lower hospitalization expenses. In addition, fundus-adjacent puncture was associated with a 11.93 min reduction in LC operative time, although the association did not reach statistical significance (95%CI - 24.40 to 0.54; P = 0.061). Conclusions PTGD with puncture site adjacent to the gallbladder fundus is associated with improved surgical efficiency and reduced postoperative burden during subsequent LC. These findings suggest that fundus-adjacent puncture may be a favorable approach in clinical practice for optimizing patient outcomes following PTGD when technically feasible and clinically appropriate.

title: Leveraging traditional and advanced machine learning for comprehensive oncology data integration and outcome prediction.
abstract: Background Outcome prediction in neuro-oncology remains challenging due to heterogeneity in tumor biology, imaging characteristics, treatment response, and patient-specific clinical factors. Although molecular databases have advanced understanding of brain tumor biology, many datasets lack broader data necessary for generalizable predictive modeling. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly being explored to integrate these heterogeneous data sources and support precision neuro-oncology. Methods A narrative review was performed using PubMed and Embase to identify studies evaluating oncology databases, ML models, multimodal data integration, and AI applications relevant to neuro-oncology. Studies published between 2020 and 2026 were preferentially reviewed, with additional landmark studies included when relevant. Results Traditional ML approaches including regression-based models, random forests, support vector machines, and gradient boosting algorithms have been applied to survival prediction, recurrence classification, treatment response estimation, and molecular biomarker prediction using clinical, imaging, molecular, and population-level datasets. More advanced architectures including natural language processing, large language models, vision transformers, geometric deep learning, and graph neural networks have expanded the ability to analyze unstructured and multimodal data sources including radiology reports, histopathology slides, MRI volumes, molecular datasets, and electronic health records. Multimodal AI systems integrating imaging, molecular, histopathologic, clinical, and socioeconomic data frequently demonstrated improved predictive performance compared with single-modality models. However, widespread clinical implementation remains limited by dataset heterogeneity, limited external validation, interpretability concerns, and inconsistent representation across patient populations. Conclusions AI and ML approaches are increasingly capable of integrating complex neuro-oncology datasets in ways that more closely reflect real-world clinical decision-making. Although most current models remain investigational, multimodal AI frameworks may ultimately improve prognostic assessment, treatment stratification, and precision neuro-oncology care. Continued progress will require larger representative datasets, improved data harmonization, external validation, and clinically interpretable models.

title: RDB CycleGAN-CBAM: an integrated deep learning model for low-dose ct image denoising.
abstract: Computed Tomography (CT) is one of the largest contributors to radiation exposure from medical imaging, which can induce DNA damage and increase cancer risk. Reducing CT radiation dose to improve patient safety inherently increases image noise and artifacts. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) have shown promise for unsupervised low-dose CT (LDCT) denoising. Building on this, RDBCycleGAN-CBAM, a CycleGAN-based model that integrates residual dense blocks (RDBs) and convolutional block attention modules (CBAM), was developed to effectively denoise quarter-dose CT images while preserving structural detail. The model was trained on unpaired quarter-dose and full-dose CT scans from the NIH-AAPM-Mayo dataset using adversarial (LSGAN), cycle-consistency, and identity losses. Evaluation on held-out test slices was performed using PSNR and SSIM as the primary image-quality metrics. The results demonstrate that the proposed RDBCycleGAN-CBAM method demonstrated improvements that were competitive with values reported in previous studies, achieving mean improvements of + 3.973 dB in PSNR and + 0.053 in SSIM relative to quarter-dose inputs. Shapiro-Wilk tests for PSNR and SSIM motivated the use of the nonparametric Wilcoxon signed-rank test, by which highly significant improvements across both metrics (PSNR and SSIM) were demonstrated. The very large rank-biserial correlation values (1.0) indicate that nearly all test images experienced substantial quality improvement. Furthermore, the narrow bootstrap confidence intervals for the mean differences suggest that these improvements are consistent across the dataset. These findings support further investigation of RDBCycleGAN-CBAM as a vendor-neutral image-domain denoising approach, while external validation and reader studies are required to establish its clinical utility and potential for dose reduction.

title: Learning from the unseen: synthetic data for scoliosis AI segmentation.
abstract: Purpose Severe scoliosis remains challenging for 3D vertebral segmentation because annotated pathological computed tomography (CT) data are scarce. Methods We synthesize scoliosis-like CT volumes by jointly warping public healthy spine scans and labels and then train nnU-Net CNN and PRIMUS models under matched compute. We evaluate on in-house out-of-distribution (OOD) adolescent scoliosis CTs and the public Spine1K dataset. Results On 18 in-house adolescent scoliosis CTs, the best CNN setting increased mean Dice from 0.765 to 0.842 and vertebra success rate from 73.2 to 81.6%. In 55 surgeon-defined apical labels, mean Dice increased from 0.720 to 0.854. Spine1K performance remained high when synthetic data supplemented real scans; synthetic-only training was less stable. Conclusion Pathology-informed synthetic data improve robustness to severe scoliosis without new annotations or architecture changes. Code and interactive visualizations are available at: https://chepchikvaleri.github.io/synth-data-s/.
originalAbstract:
Purpose

Severe scoliosis remains challenging for 3D vertebral segmentation because annotated pathological computed tomography (CT) data are scarce.

Methods

We synthesize scoliosis-like CT volumes by jointly warping public healthy spine scans and labels and then train nnU-Net CNN and PRIMUS models under matched compute. We evaluate on in-house out-of-distribution (OOD) adolescent scoliosis CTs and the public Spine1K dataset.

Results

On 18 in-house adolescent scoliosis CTs, the best CNN setting increased mean Dice from 0.765 to 0.842 and vertebra success rate from 73.2 to 81.6%. In 55 surgeon-defined apical labels, mean Dice increased from 0.720 to 0.854. Spine1K performance remained high when synthetic data supplemented real scans; synthetic-only training was less stable.

Conclusion

Pathology-informed synthetic data improve robustness to severe scoliosis without new annotations or architecture changes. Code and interactive visualizations are available at: https://chepchikvaleri.github.io/synth-data-s/.

title: The clinical application value of mixed reality guidance in robot-assisted laparoscopic radical nephrectomy for renal cancer.
abstract: Although robot-assisted laparoscopic radical nephrectomy (RAL-RN) has realized the benefits of minimally invasive surgery, it continues to face several key technical limitations, including the lack of integrated patient-specific three-dimensional anatomical navigation and insufficient real-time intraoperative navigation. While mixed reality (MR) technology has shown considerable potential in renal tumor surgery, its clinical application value specifically within the context of radical nephrectomy for renal cancer warrants further systematic evaluation. This study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy and practical value of MR guidance in RAL-RN. A retrospective analysis was conducted of 74 patients who underwent RAL-RN between September 2021 and March 2024. Participants were categorized into two groups based on preoperative assessment methodology: an MR navigation group (n = 33) and a conventional imaging group (n = 41). All patients received non-contrast and triple-phase contrast-enhanced renal CT scans. The MR group utilized Hololens-based intraoperative anatomical reference with three-dimensional models reconstructed from preoperative CT data during Da Vinci robotic procedures. Perioperative outcomes, including baseline demographic and clinical characteristics, operative time, estimated blood loss, and postoperative complications, were compared between the two groups to assess the potential technical advantages of MR-guided navigation. The two groups showed comparable baseline characteristics (p > 0.05). The MR group exhibited significantly shorter operative time (161.15 ± 10.87 min versus 182.29 ± 12.40 min, p < 0.001), reduced blood loss (150.00 mL [interquartile range 140.00 to 165.00] versus 165.00 mL [150.00 to 165.00], p = 0.008), faster gastrointestinal function recovery (26.82 ± 4.17 h versus 28.93 ± 3.68 h, p = 0.024), earlier tube removal (5.00 days [4.00 to 5.00] versus 6.00 days [6.00 to 7.00], p < 0.001), and shorter postoperative hospitalization (6.00 days [6.00 to 7.00] versus 8.00 days [7.00 to 8.00], p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in tumor staging, renal function parameters (postoperative and 12-month Scr and GFR), histopathological type, or complication rates (Clavien-Dindo grades 1 and 2) between groups (all p > 0.05). MR guidance was associated with shorter operative time and faster postoperative recovery in RAL-RN. However, given the non-randomized design, these findings should be regarded as preliminary and cannot establish causality. Prospective studies with standardized allocation and adequate follow-up are warranted to confirm the clinical value of MR guidance.
